title: Bayern Munich among top five clubs to be compensated by FIFA following World Cup
description: A lot of risk, less reward?
fullText:
The relationship between club and international football has always been shaky at best. Clubs fear injuries that could derail an entire season while international teams pine for their nation’s top talents — a complex conflict of interest.

Nowhere is the conflict as prominent as the FIFA World Cup. Clubs have no choice but to surrender their talent to their national teams. The hesitancy isn’t a product of not wanting players to represent their countries on the world’s greatest stage. It is rather a matter of risk.

Already fatigued after a long season of club football, players are at a heightened risk of injury — not to mention the select few who decide to play through afflictions for the pride of representing their country at the World Cup. Germany’s Lennart Karl and Nico Schlotterbeck suffered tournament-ending injuries, while Belgium’s Amadou Onana sustained a torn ACL mid-tournament. Argentinian pair Facundo Medina and Lisandro Martínez both face an extended stint on the sidelines, England’s Tino Livramento picked up a fresh setback in a long line of past injuries, and Morocco’s Abde Ezzalzouli was ruled out for six weeks after injuring his knee.

Among other reasons, to make up for the immense risk FIFA offers compensation for clubs whose players feature at the World Cup.

According to Kicker (via @iMiaSanMia), Bayern Munich is one of the clubs that will benefit the most.

Compensation payments paid out by FIFA to clubs for releasing their players for the World Cup:

1- Manchester City €3.08m
2- PSG €2.49m
3- Arsenal €2.42m
4- Bayern €2.3m
5- Barcelona €2.2m
6- Chelsea €2.12m

Whether the compensation provided by FIFA truly outweighs the extra kilometres players clock and a heightened risk of injury is up for debate. But, the fact that there is compensation — a luxury that didn’t always exist — is a step in the right direction.

title: 'Mind-blowing' El Niño stuns scientists. Why are they so concerned?
description: A Pacific El Niño is setting daily warm water records. Scientists say the world is in uncharted waters, and they aren't sure what will happen next.
fullText:
The world's most influential climate pattern is baring its teeth in the Pacific.

The strengthening El Niño – a natural warming of seawater that influences weather around the planet – is setting daily warm water records.

It's not only "very likely to be the strongest event since reliable records began – it may end up the strongest by a truly mind-blowing margin," Zeke Hausfather, a research scientist at Berkeley Earth, wrote in a post for The Climate Brink, a Substack blog, earlier in July.

It remains to be seen what this will mean for the world's weather over the next 12 to 18 months, but climate scientists say El Niño's effects on global temperatures will increase the chances that 2026 could be the warmest year on record, and make it likely that 2027 will be the warmest.

Meanwhile, world leaders have expressed concern about the prospect of droughts, heavy rainfall events and heat waves. (It's worth noting, however, that not all El Niño effects are sinister. The climate pattern is widely expected to tame the 2026 Atlantic Hurricane season.)

Economy: 'Super El Niño' will have an alarming financial impact, experts fear

El Niño impacts are already being felt in the U.S., suppressing Atlantic hurricane activity and bringing unusual heat and humidity to parts of California, one of the states most vulnerable to El Niño's impacts.

Sea surface temperatures already have crossed the threshold that typically marks a very strong event, Hausfather and Robert Rohde, his colleague at Berkeley Earth, wrote in a monthly climate briefing on July 23.

The warming trajectory of sea surface temperatures in the El Niño region along the equator has been "remarkable," developing faster than the 1997-98 El Niño, Hausfather wrote in the earlier post.

NOAA data shows water temperatures in the region have never run this hot in July in the modern record.

While El Niño is a naturally occurring pattern, concerns are growing about its amplified impacts when combined with the climate change-fueled warmer-than-normal temperatures around the globe.

The world is looking at "an unprecedented combination" between the strong El Niño and the elevated warmth from climate change, said Daniel Swain, a climate scientist with the University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources. That will influence what El Niño actually means on the ground in the U.S. and across the world, Swain said.

Previous El Niño events temporarily raised global temperatures about 0.54 degrees Fahrenheit, he said. Now the globe will have the effects of long-term human-caused warming with additional warming on top of that.

"A potentially record-breaking El Niño on top of record-breaking global temperatures to begin with is a pretty big deal," he said.

"The odds of either this year or next year, or both, setting a new record warm average global temperature are high," Swain said. "If we don't get there this year, we almost certainly will next year."

Sea surface temperatures in the El Niño region of the Pacific are up to 6 degrees warmer than normal for the date, a phenomenon that is several times more likely because of climate change, according to Climate Central, a nonprofit climate science and communications organization.

"What is most striking is how strong this event is forecast to become," wrote Hausfather and Rohde in their briefing. The vast majority of computer models predict an El Niño that exceeds the 2015-2016 record event, even taking into account the background ocean warming, the pair concluded. It's "more likely than not to be the strongest El Niño ever observed."

A "very strong" El Niño can influence weather worldwide.

"El Niño will give an extra boost to global temperatures," stated Alvaro Silva, a World Meteorological Organization scientist. "We know that during El Niño years, the global temperatures normally reach record levels."

In the U.S., a strong El Niño means "a pretty robust increase in the jet stream," Swain said. "That can result in more intense and more frequent winter storms in California, the interior southwest and the southern tier of states."

"Some of California's wettest winters have occurred during some of the strongest El Niños," he said.

El Niño can heighten hurricane activity in the eastern Pacific and suppress hurricane activity in the Atlantic.

Because of its influence on hydrologic cycles, El Niño can bring catastrophic floods to some regions but severe drought and wildfires to others. It can also disrupt fisheries and food production and bring about trillions of dollars in economic losses.

"The current forecasts imply this could be the costliest El Niño on record," Justin Mankin, a Dartmouth geography associate professor who studies El Niño's economic impacts, recently told USA TODAY by email.

Specifically, there are likely to be drier-than-average conditions in Central America and the Caribbean, along with North and South America, the United Nations said. Drier weather patterns are also forecast in parts of Indonesia and Southeast Asia during the monsoon season, but wetter conditions are anticipated during the rainy season from September to December in East Africa.

Even though the signals and models point to a strong El Niño, that doesn't mean it will definitely be the strongest on record when it's expected to peak later this year, said climate scientist Michael Mann, director of the Penn Center for Science, Sustainability & the Media at the University of Pennsylvania.

"It's clear we are headed towards an historically strong event," Mann said, but "there's still a variety of scenarios we could see."

El Niño is intrinsically a chaotic event in a climate system that doesn't always respond in simple, proportional ways, Mann explained. Its greatest impacts come from its connections to the larger atmosphere, such as the trade winds and upper atmospheric winds, but those teleconnections can be hard to predict.

Small differences in conditions such as ocean temperatures or the trade winds can alter what happens later. For example, El Niño's ultimate impacts depend on factors such as where the maximum heating takes place in the equatorial Pacific in the fall and early winter.

Part of the uncertainty rests with the fact that the models are in "uncharted waters," Hausfather wrote. The models have "never been verified in this territory."

It's unusual to see this kind of agreement among the strongest predictive models, but what that will mean remains to be seen, Swain said. "Every event has a different flavor and this will undoubtedly have a different flavor than we've ever seen before."

Dinah Voyles Pulver and Doyle Rice are national correspondents with USA TODAY who have decades of experience writing about weather and climate. Reach them at dpulver@usatoday.com and drice@usatoday.com.

title: Bloodied Kelly battles past Agyarko to retain title
description: Briton Josh Kelly is forced to dig deep to retain his IBF light-middleweight world title in a points win against Ireland's Caoimhin Agyarko.
fullText:
Briton Josh Kelly was forced to dig deep to retain his IBF light-middleweight world title, surviving a spirited late comeback from Belfast's Caoimhin Agyarko to win a narrow points decision in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Kelly looked in complete control until the complexion of the contest changed when he received a deserved sixth-round point deduction for repeated punches to the back of the head.

The 31-year-old was then bloodied by cuts across his face and a gash on his nose as Agyarko grew in confidence and began to land with increasing success.

But Kelly stood firm through the championship rounds to secure victory, with the judges scoring the contest 114-113, 115-112 and 115-112.

"That was a messy and hard fight. I didn't get cuts from punches like this, it comes from heads and elbows. This is what it looks like when you've got tight skin," Kelly said.

"I knew he [Agyarko] was go to be tricky and awkward. [He had] a good game plan. He tried to make it a good boxing match. I had to show a different side to me at the end and that is what a champions does."

Fighting on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's heavyweight comeback against Kristian Prenga, Sunderland's Kelly claimed his 21st professional victory.

Agyarko, 29, had hoped to become Ireland's first black world champion. Instead, despite a brave second-half comeback, he suffered the first defeat of his professional career in his 30th contest.

Also on the card, WBO super-middleweight champion Hamzah Sheeraz laboured to an underwhelming points win over Simon Zachenhuber.

The 27-year-old Briton was far from his best and struggled to find his rhythm but was awarded a majority decision as he extended his record to 24 wins and one defeat.

Agyarko 'didn't do enough' in world title defeat

The tension between the pair had simmered all week, threatening to boil over at Friday's weigh-in after Kelly vowed to "humiliate" his opponent.

Kelly started with a spring in his step, dropping his hands, smiling and chatting to Agyarko as he controlled the opening exchanges.

The challenger was already showing swelling under his right eye by the second round as Kelly began to let his hands go, firing in sharp combinations.

Fresh from winning the IBF title with a points victory over Bakhram Murtazaliev in January, Kelly looked every inch a confident champion. Agyarko had moments with his jab but struggled to match the champion's speed and movement.

Kelly unloaded with a flurry in the fifth, but the point deduction disrupted his rhythm and Agyarko, renowned for finishing strongly, began to find success with left hooks.

A head clash in the ninth round left Kelly with a cut on his nose. "He doesn't want it," Agyarko's corner shouted in the 10th but Kelly responded with sharp uppercuts.

The final two rounds were tense, with Kelly landing the cleaner work before catching Agyarko with a double left hook in the 12th.

Fighting just two months after stopping Alem Begic to win the vacant WBO title, Londoner Sheeraz controlled the early rounds and landed heavy body shots in the second and third.

But German Zachenhuber, 28, who arrived with a 29-1 record built largely against limited opposition, began to frustrate the champion with his southpaw stance.

Sheeraz walked his opponent down but struggled to find the spite and power that had stopped 19 of his previous 24 opponents.

"I will press him," Sheeraz told trainer Andy Lee, but despite winning every round to that point he appeared reluctant to let his right hand go.

A left hook to the body followed by an uppercut hurt Zachenhuber in the ninth, but Sheeraz could not capitalise.

The scorecards were closer than many expected, with one judge scoring the fight a draw. But cards of 114-114, 115-113 and 116-112 handed Sheeraz a majority decision victory.

"I knew it wasn't good but I didn't think it was that bad," Sheeraz said, dismissing suggestions of any injury to his right hand.

After a hard-fought win, Kelly's attention can now turn to the marquee names in their divisions.

While Sebastian Fundora holds the WBA title, Kelly has set his sights on fellow Matchroom fighter Jaron 'Boots' Ennis.

The unbeaten American is a two-weight world champion and the WBA and WBO light-middleweight champion, boasting 32 stoppages in 36 victories.

"I want it next," Kelly said. "People will be smiling looking at that and saying 'what is he talking about' - but that style of fight is a tricky night for anyone.

"I want the big names in the division. I have already took out one big name in Bakhram Murtazaliev. Let me get the other ones."

Sheeraz, meanwhile, remains in contention for a lucrative match-up against Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez.

The Mexican superstar, who has beaten all eight Britons he has faced, must first get past Christian Mbilli in October for the WBC belt before any potential unification showdown can be discussed.

"I'm sure people are chomping at the bit after that performance, so let's make the big ones happen," Sheeraz said.

title: Vozinha to join Chilean club after World Cup heroics
description: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who earned plaudits for his feats during the World Cup, is set to join Chilean side Colo Colo.
fullText:
Vozinha, the Cape Verde goalkeeper who earned plaudits for his World Cup performances, is set to join Chilean side Colo Colo.

The 40-year-old headed to the World Cup without a club after his contract with Portuguese second division side Chaves expired, but he became an overnight sensation by starring in a goalless draw against eventual champions Spain.

He has now found a new club, according to Colo Colo president Anibal Mosa.

"Vozinha will be a Colo Colo player," said Mosa.

"In the coming days he will travel to Chile, undergo the usual medical examinations and then be presented here at the Estadio Monumental."

Mosa said Vozinha's World Cup displays showed he deserved the move, acknowledging the signing also carried marketing appeal for Colo Colo.

The club, based in the Chilean capital of Santiago, sit top of Liga de Primera - the country's top division.

New species named after Cape Verde keeper Vozinha

Underdogs, history and late goals - Africa's World Cup

Although the transfer has yet to be finalised, the club teased the signing on social media, external with an image showing Vozinha's familiar curly hair.

The experienced keeper become a cult hero and attracted millions of new followers on social media after Cape Verde claimed their first-ever World Cup point against Spain in the group stage.

Cape Verde, the second smallest nation to ever reach the World Cup finals, went close to upsetting Argentina in the last 32 before exiting the competition with a 3-2 extra-time defeat by Lionel Messi and co, who began the tournament as holders and went on to reach another final.

Vozinha has previously played club football in Slovakia, Angola, Moldova, Cyprus and Portugal.

title: Littler sets up Price final at World Matchplay
description: Luke Littler is on course to beat Phil Taylor's tournament average record after another impressive victory saw him reach the final.
fullText:
Defending champion Luke Littler strolled into the World Matchplay final with a 17-5 demolition of unseeded Dirk van Duijvenbode in Blackpool.

The world number one raced in an 8-2 advantage and was averaging 117.10 and on course to beat Phil Taylor's tournament match average record of 114.99

Littler admitted afterwards that distracted him and his level did drop slightly as he finished with an average just below 111.

However, that leaves him well placed to beat Taylor's tournament average of 106.31, with Littler's currently at 110.88.

The teenager's victory also means he has now amassed more than £3m in the PDC's order of merit, and is more than £2m clear of world number two Luke Humphries.

Littler will face Wales' Gerwyn Price in Sunday's final after he beat Netherlands' Gian van Veen 17-10.

Sunday's final gets under way at 20:05 BST, with the Women's World Matchplay taking place in the afternoon session from 13:00 – Beau Greaves and defending champion Lisa Ashton the top two seeds.

Littler has averaged more than 109 in all four matches in this year's tournament as he looks to join Taylor and Michael van Gerwen as the only back-to-back winners of the Matchplay.

The run is also continuing his sublime form in longer-format matches - this win extending the streak to 28 successive wins in games with 20 or more legs.

His last defeat over a match of that duration was when he burst on to the scene in the 2024 World Championship and lost to Luke Humphries in the final.

That gives an indication of the challenge that Price will face on Sunday in his second Matchplay final.

The pair have a bit of rivalry with Price's on-stage roars and antics often provoking Littler into doing similar, but the teenager denied that Price can get "under his skin".

Earlier in the week, Price said that some players can "make it too easy" for Littler.

Despite their battles, Littler has won the past nine encounters between the pair, with Price's last success in their opening meeting of 2026.

The Welshman has never beat Littler in a game that has contained more than 15 legs so will have to reach new heights in the best-of-35 final.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Littler said: "Me and Gez always have great games. Gez will want to try and get me into a roaring battle. As long as I can get into the lead that will be the thing."

Price broke in the opening leg of the game and charged into a 4-1 lead, before a scrappy run of legs saw both players break throw regularly to leave Price leading 11-9 at the final mini-break.

From there, the seventh seed powered on and stretched away from Van Veen in scoring and finishing to seal a comfortable victory.

Both players missed 23 darts at a double across the match, while Van Veen was broken nine times in 14 legs throwing first on what was a difficult night for the world number three.

The victory sees Price climb to fourth in the order of merit, above Jonny Clayton, and in turn becomes Welsh number one.

Price told Sky Sports he was "happy" to reach the final, but "getting one up" on good friend Clayton was his main focus going into the tie.

title: Messi can skip All-Star Game after grueling World Cup, says MLS
description: Lionel Messi will not be required to play in next week's Major League Soccer All-Star Game after representing Argentina in the recent World Cup final, the US domestic league said Saturday."Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Major League Soccer and the MLS Players Association agreed that upon a player's exit from the World Cup competition, clubs would have individual conversations with each player to determine the appropriate rest and return to training and competition timeline," said the sta
fullText:
Lionel Messi will not be required to play in next week's Major League Soccer All-Star Game after representing Argentina in the recent World Cup final, the US domestic league said Saturday.

Inter Miami superstar Messi had been sanctioned last year for skipping the annual showcase, which pits top players from across MLS against rivals from the Mexican Liga-MX.

Participation is usually mandatory, with exceptions for injury.

But this year, the World Cup took place in the middle of the MLS season, which paused for a seven-week break, and the league confirmed exceptions had been pre-arranged for players reaching the international tournament's final stages.

"Prior to the start of the 2026 season, Major League Soccer and the MLS Players Association agreed that upon a player's exit from the World Cup competition, clubs would have individual conversations with each player to determine the appropriate rest and return to training and competition timeline," said the statement.

"Consistent with that agreement, Rodrigo De Paul and Lionel Messi will be excused from participating in the 2026 MLS All-Star Game."

Fellow Argentine De Paul also featured in last Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time.

Messi had been among the first 11 players named to the MLS squad for this year's All-Star Game, which takes place in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Wednesday.

In his absence, stars will include Los Angeles FC's Son Heung-min, the Vancouver Whitecaps' Thomas Muller, and US national team captain Tim Ream, who plays for Charlotte.

Last year, Messi and then-Inter Miami teammate Jordi Alba were slapped with a one-game suspension for skipping the All-Star Game at the last minute.

MLS commissioner Don Garber at the time expressed sympathy for Messi's grueling schedule, saying it had been a "very difficult decision" and that the league's long-standing All-Star Game policy would be reviewed.

Nonetheless, Inter Miami's billionaire co-owner Jorge Mas said Messi was "very upset" by the suspension.

description: Como have recently submitted an offer to Chelsea in an attempt to sign England international Trevoh Chalobah, but the latest updates confirm that their bid has been turned down by the Premier League s...
fullText:
Como have recently submitted an offer to Chelsea in an attempt to sign England international Trevoh Chalobah, but the latest updates confirm that their bid has been turned down by the Premier League side.

According to reports from various outlets on Saturday, Como had submitted an offer worth a guaranteed €25m plus €5m in easily-achievable bonuses to take the deal up to the €30m mark.

However, according to the latest updates from Fabrizio Romano, Chelsea have informed Como that they will need to up their bid beyond the €30m if they are to strike an agreement.

LONDON, ENGLAND – FEBRUARY 21: Trevoh Chalobah of Chelsea during the Premier League match between Chelsea and Burnley at Stamford Bridge on February 21, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Saturday’s report adds that Como are still weighing up other profiles to strengthen Cesc Fabregas’s back line, but that Chalobah is still keen on the move and is still likely to leave Chelsea this summer.

Inter had also briefly been linked with a move for the Chelsea academy product, but recent reports indicate that they are pursuing a move for Tottenham’s Cristian Romero instead.

title: A Visual Guide to the Hierarchical Navigable Small World Algorithm
description: Explore the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm through interactive visualizations and demos, providing an in-depth understanding of its mechanics and applications in similarity search.
fullText:
This post is part two in this series about similarity search. To read the first part of this series, check out A Visual Guide to Vector Search and K-Nearest Neighbors.

░ NOTE
░ The text, code examples, and the visualizations in this article are works-in-progress.

We’ll dive into the inner workings of an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithm called Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW). HNSW is commonly used algorithm in vector databases to enhance the speed of similarity search. Throughout this article, we’ll use interactive visuals and demos to demonstrate the fundamental concepts of the HNSW algorithm.

Hierarchical NSW is one of several approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms developed to speed up similarity search. Initially proposed by Yu. A. Malkov and
D. A. Yashunin in 2016, HNSW builds on the concept of two other algorithms:

Combining both, HNSW generates a multi-layer NSW graph that enables a logarithmic time complexity for approximate nearest neighbor search. Its performance was significantly better compared to previous state-of-the-art ANN algorithms.

Mastering the concepts of skip lists and navigable small world data structures is a prerequisite for comprehending the inner workings of HNSW. This understanding will serve as a solid foundation for our exploration of HNSW.

An example below demonstrates searching for a node valued 5 in a Skip List.

Skip Lists enhance singly linked lists by introducing multiple layers, with each node having a randomly assigned height. Unlike traditional linked lists where each node points to the next, Skip List nodes have multiple pointers for different layers. The node’s height, indicating its layer stack, ranges from a dense, fully connected, bottom layer to a sparse top layer.
This multi-layered approach allows for efficient element “skipping” during searches

Node heights in a skip list are probabilistically assigned on insertion of a node, with each additional layer usually having a halved chance of inclusion, with the probability p being set to a default value of 0.5. This means a node’s height is akin to flipping a coin: a head adds another layer, while a tail stops the process, making taller nodes less common as layers increase.

This results in a structure with multiple levels, with the top level containing the sparsest amount of nodes and the bottom level being the most dense.
The lowest level contains all the elements like a regular linked list, except ordered. Inserts and searches on a skip list have an average time complexity of O(log n), compared to O(n) linear time for a linked list.

This unique structure enables the “skipping” of elements during search, which is the property that gives skip lists performance advantages over traditional linked lists and a similar performance profile to balanced trees.

Play with the interactive demo below to see how this skipping works in practice to speed up search:

The animation above shows a Skip List search for a node with value 5.
The search starts at the top level, comparing the target value with adjacent nodes.
If the target matches or is less than the next node, the search moves to that node.
Otherwise, if the next node’s value is greater or it’s the end of the list, the search drops to the next lower level.
This process repeats until the desired node is found at the lowest level.

This method is significantly faster than a standard linear search in a linked list. The Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm applies a similar concept to gain performance improvements during search and insertion, but using a graph instead of a linked list.

Navigable Small World (NSW) provides a method for constructing and traversing a graph that facilitates fast approximate nearest neighbor search. A greedy search of this graph has a polylogarithmic time complexity of O(logᵏn), which can be faster than the linear time complexity of a naive KNN search.

The NSW graph employs a strategy known as greedy routing during search and insertion. The search process in NSW commences by selecting an entry point.

Typically the entry point is the first node ever inserted. Early nodes typically remain a starting point because long-range edges are likely to be created during the initial graph construction phase. These edges play a vital role in graph navigation. They serve as bridges between network hubs, maintaining overall graph connectivity and enabling logarithmic scaling of the number of hops during greedy routing.

The algorithm then takes the set of all of the neighbors of the current node (a.k.a the neighborhood) plus the current node itself and computes the distances between the elements of this set with the
query vector (the vector we are trying to find similar vectors to). If a node closer to the query vector is found among that set, that node becomes the current node, and the process continues
at that node. The search procedure concludes when the algorithm cannot find a neighbor node closer to the query than the current node itself. This node is then returned as the response to the query.

However, this greedy strategy does not guarantee the discovery of the best nearest neighbor as it uses only local information at each step to make decisions. One of the properties of this algorithm is early stopping,
which happens when an iteration finds no better neighbor nodes than the current one. This property is what gives NSW its improved performance compared to naive search, but runs the risk that the node returned is only
a local minimum instead of the global minimum.

To mitigate this local minima problem, NSW can employ multiple searches from different random starting points (called multi-search counts), combining results to find better approximate nearest neighbors. However, this approach requires running the search algorithm multiple times, which increases computational cost.

The insertion process mirrors the search process, tracing the same path it would have taken if it were a search query. It establishes connections to its K nearest vertices upon reaching a local minimum.

The demo below demonstrates this process. It begins running automatically, but you can pause it to manually add nodes and perform searches to better understand how the algorithm operates.

Using the demo, here’s an interesting challenge: see if you can generate an example of early stopping, where the node returned from the search is not actually the closet node but a local minima.

The HNSW is essentially a NSW and a skip list combined, forming a multi layer NSW. Similar to a skip list, whenever a node is added to the graph, it is assigned a height probabilistically. Having multiple layers means that each node in the graph will not just have one set of neighbors, but actually a set of neighbors for each level they are on.

The below interactive demonstration of HNSW shows how search is conducted. Pay attention to how search is conducted at each layer, with a neighborhood being constructed to find closer nodes at the current layer. The query node is highlighted in yellow. The current node will be the one with the animated dark blue/red border. Neighborhood search of nodes will highlight neighbors with a light blue fill. The most similar nodes returned from the search will be highlighted yellow.

The Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm enhances the Navigable Small World (NSW) model with several key improvements. Unlike NSW, which relies on multi-search counts to improve accuracy, HNSW employs the ef parameter (effective search size) for more refined control over search precision. The algorithm also introduces a heuristic approach to selecting neighbors that considers spatial distribution to prevent clustering, rather than merely choosing the closest neighbors. Finally, HNSW adds optimization parameters like mLm_L for level generation and Mmax0M_{\text{max0}} for maximum connections, which together optimize graph construction while maintaining navigability.

When searching for k nearest neighbors in an existing HNSW graph, the algorithm starts at the entry point (the node with the highest layer) and performs a greedy graph traversal downward through the layers. At each layer, it explores neighbors of the current node, always moving to whichever neighbor is closest to the query point. This greedy search continues until no neighbor is closer than the current node—a local minimum at that layer.

At upper layers (all layers above layer 0), the algorithm uses ef=1, meaning it maintains only the single closest node found during traversal. This closest node at each layer becomes the starting point for the search at the next layer down. Once a local minimum is found at a layer, the search descends to the next layer down and continues the greedy traversal.

At layer 0 (the bottom layer), the search strategy changes. The ef parameter increases to the desired search quality value, allowing the algorithm to maintain a list of multiple candidates instead of just one. The larger the ef value, the more candidates the algorithm explores, improving accuracy at the cost of speed. The search returns the k closest nodes found. This architecture brings down the complexity of search operations to O(log(n)) on average.

While search and insertion follow similar traversal patterns, they differ in how they use the ef parameter. When inserting a new node and building the graph, the algorithm again begins at the entry point at the highest layer and performs greedy graph traversal downward. However, the ef parameter behavior is different from search.

The traversal starts at the top layer and works downward. At each layer, the algorithm explores the graph by examining neighbors of the current node, always moving to whichever neighbor is closest to the new node being inserted. This greedy search continues until no neighbor is closer than the current node—a local minimum at that layer.

The search strategy changes depending on which layers the new node will occupy. Each node is assigned a maximum layer during insertion through probabilistic selection. If a new node is assigned to layer 2, it will exist in layers 0, 1, and 2. For layers above where the new node will exist, the algorithm uses ef=1, meaning it only tracks the single closest node found during traversal. This closest node at each layer becomes the starting point for the search at the next layer down.

Once the traversal reaches a layer where the new node will exist, the search strategy shifts. The ef parameter increases to efConstruction (a larger value), allowing the algorithm to maintain a list of multiple candidate neighbors instead of just one. The algorithm continues this broader search through each remaining layer down to layer 0.

At each layer where the new node exists, it gets connected to M neighbors selected from the candidates found during traversal. The selection of which M neighbors to connect is where the simple versus heuristic approaches differ. This architecture brings down the complexity of insertion operations to O(log(n)) on average.

The HNSW paper presents two methods for selecting which M neighbors to connect when inserting a new node.

The simple selection method chooses the M closest nodes from the candidates found during traversal. This approach is computationally efficient and works well for most datasets. Our interactive demonstration uses this method.

The heuristic method aims to improve graph connectivity by considering both distance and diversity when selecting neighbors. Rather than always choosing the M closest nodes, it may select some slightly farther nodes if they provide connections to different regions of the graph. This helps prevent isolated clusters and dead ends. The heuristic also uses different connection limits: MmaxM_{\text{max}} for upper layers and Mmax0M_{\text{max0}} (typically 2×M2 \times M) for the base layer, with pruning when these limits are exceeded.

Beyond neighbor selection, several key parameters control how the hierarchical graph structure is built. Like skip lists, each node’s layer assignment is determined probabilistically when inserted. A node inserted at layer ll appears in all layers from 0 up to ll. The layer assignment follows an exponential decay distribution:

The parameter mLm_L acts as a normalization factor controlling how many nodes appear in higher layers. A smaller mLm_L means fewer nodes in upper layers, creating a steeper hierarchy. Different parameter combinations affect search complexity:

The choice of mLm_L involves a trade-off. Smaller values reduce overlap between neighbor lists across layers, improving graph navigability. However, this also means fewer nodes per layer, requiring more traversal hops. A good choice for mLm_L is 1/ln⁡(M)1/\ln(M), analogous to the skip list parameter p=1/Mp = 1/M.

Another parameter MM controls how many bi-directional connections each node can have. The maximum connections at layer 0 is controlled by Mmax0M_{\text{max0}}, a separate parameter commonly set to M⋅2M \cdot 2 to maintain strong graph connectivity at the base layer. Typical MM values range from 5 to 48, with higher values improving recall at the cost of memory and insertion time. During construction, the efConstructionefConstruction parameter controls search quality - higher values produce better graphs but take longer to build.

Hierarchical NSW (HNSW) improves on K-ANN search by leveraging structure decomposition and smart neighbor selection. This approach not only addresses the limitations of basic NSW but also sets new benchmarks in performance, especially with high-dimensional data.

title: Beaugrand and Hauser take London triathlon wins as GB miss out
description: Cassandre Beaugrand and Matt Hauser claim their third win of this year's World Triathlon Championship Series.
fullText:
Cassandre Beaugrand and Matt Hauser both claimed a third win in this year's World Triathlon Championship Series in London, where British hopes were hindered by crashes on the bike.

Tilly Anema was unable to continue after hitting a cone while part of a lead duo, while fellow Briton Alex Yee was a minute down on a 13-man lead group before he got tangled up in a crash shortly before the second transition.

Olympic champion Yee produced the quickest time for the run - his strongest discipline - but that gained only 17 seconds on Hauser and Vasco Vilaca, who put on a thrilling sprint finish in the men's race.

World champion Hauser won in 50 minutes 28 seconds, with Portugal's Vilaca three seconds behind the Australian on a course consisting of a 750m swim, 20km bike ride and 5km run.

Hungary's Csongor Lehmann was third - eight seconds behind Hauser - while Yee was more than a minute back in 14th and compatriot Max Stapley 12th.

Olympic champion Beaugrand won the women's race in 56mins 6secs, five seconds ahead of Germany's Lisa Tertsch, with Sweden's Tilda Mansson 15 seconds adrift.

Beth Potter and Georgia Taylor-Brown were the best-placed Britons in fourth and sixth respectively as London hosted the WTCS for the first time since 2015.

Beaugrand was 27th out of the water but stayed safe in the chase group on the bike before hitting the front on the run, holding off a late challenge from world champion Tertsch.

"I had one of my worst swims ever," Beaugrand said. "I had to wake up on the bike and tried to save some energy for the run."

With two more races before the grand final, Potter still leads the women's rankings - Beaugrand is sixth - while Vilaca is the men's leader with Hauser third.

Both Vilaca and Hauser were in the lead group throughout, before Hauser pulled clear around the final two corners.

"It was nice to have another battle with Vasco and see what we had left at the end," said Hauser.

fullText:
Artificial intelligence may not deliver on its promise of vast economic opportunity at a price that humanity is willing to pay

In March, Anthropic, the cutting-edge artificial intelligence business that gave us the chatbot Claude, published an analysis on the impact of AI on employment, to help us assess the claim that intelligent robots were about to redefine human existence, ending demand for human labor.

Last year in May, Anthropic’s co-founder, Dario Amodei, claimed AI could wipe out half of all entry-level jobs in one to five years. Last January, he told us AI would probably become a “general labor substitute for humans”. In June he said we risk “a world where the economic trade-off dial is stuck on the hypergrowth, hyper-inequality setting”.

And yet, Anthropic’s report suggests that, so far, AI’s impact has fallen short of expectations: “We find no systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022,” the report stated. Deployment of the technology “remains a fraction of what’s feasible”. Claude covers just 33% of all tasks in the computer and math category whereas theoretically it could take over nearly 100% of them.

Spending on datacenters is going through the roof, for sure, but productivity has not been experiencing the galloping gains that the technorati’s epochal prognostications lead one to expect. Labor productivity was, in fact, slower in the first three years of our AI era than during the information technology boom that began in the mid 1990s.

Even OpenAI’s Sam Altman, AI’s most public face, says he now doubts its job-killing potential. “I don’t think we’re going to have the kind ​of jobs apocalypse that some of the companies in our space advocate or talk about,” he said in May. As Massachusetts Institute of Technology economist David Autor noted: “A lot of people have noticed that the world is not changing as fast as they predicted.”

This has opened the public conversation to a less cataclysmic narrative of the evolution of the technology. The emerging new story not only puts more emphasis on the complexity of the relationship between automation and human work across history. It is also raising doubts about the very feasibility of the threatened AI transformation of the universe. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index, which had been propelled almost exclusively by the rise of AI-related stocks, has fallen about 8% since its peak in early June.

One strand of critique of the “AI-will-do-everything” story might be called the O-ring argument. It comes from the mid-flight explosion of the space shuttle Challenger 73 seconds into its flight on 28 January 1986. A lengthy investigation concluded that the demise of the multibillion dollar spaceship was caused by a rubber O-ring that didn’t work at low temperatures.

That cheap O-ring proved critical. The analogy suggests that as long as AI cannot perform every task perfectly, it will increase the value of the remaining tasks. Depending on which the AI takes over, it could increase the value of high skill workers who are relieved by AI of the low-end part of their job, or increase the opportunity of lower skilled workers by taking over the more expert tasks.

As one recent study noted: “despite strong substitution at the task level, overall employment effects are modest, as reduced demand in exposed occupations is offset by productivity-driven increases in labor demand at AI-adopting firms.”

Things could change. As Jed Kolko points out, research on the labor market impact of artificial intelligence is still in its infancy. There are almost four years to go in Amodei’s one-to-five year window. And maybe devastation hits in year six. According to the Federal Reserve, adoption of AI is expanding fast across businesses.

Moreover, Autor argues, AI is getting better. And its progress shows no sign that it will soon hit a ceiling. “Skepticism about the stochastic parrot is behind us,” he told me. The dystopian AI future – utopian, if you get to own and run the AI – is still on the cards.

“Insiders are as gung ho as ever,” noted Daron Acemoglu, the Nobel prize-winning economist. “They still believe artificial general intelligence is around the corner.” Indeed, Elon Musk has not budged from the dream that “AI+Robots will be able to do everything, resulting in universal high income. Work will be optional.”

One may recall the quip by Nobel prize-winning economist Robert Solow in the early years of the computer revolution: “You can see the computer age everywhere but in the productivity statistics.” It took another 10 years or so, as businesses reorganized around the new technology. But computers did eventually show up in the stats.

Clouds are nonetheless gathering on the AI horizon. It’s not just that AI may not end all human work. AI may not deliver on its promise of vast economic opportunity at a price that humanity is willing to pay.

The politics have decidedly soured on the project. Seven in 10 Americans oppose building AI datacenters in their area. While this has to do with their insatiable demand for energy, which drives up local electricity costs, AI’s unpopularity is no doubt related to the proposition that it will destroy society as we know it.

There are other bumps in the road. Despite its vast progress, big doubts remain on whether AI can do everything a modern economy needs. “Not everything is a computational problem,” notes Autor. AI is good at replicating language, but it cannot connect language to the reality around it. Despite its progress, it still makes plenty of critical mistakes.

And then there are the impossible economics. Even if AI could eventually solve all our problems, the solution looks expensive. How much of GDP are we willing to invest in AI datacenters, 20%? 30%? 40%? According to some estimates, that is where we are headed. The International Energy Agency estimates that power demand from datacenters will more than double by 2030 to about 945 terawatt-hours, more than the energy consumption of Japan.

The economics look more fragile considering how fast the investment in AI depreciates, as new models overtake those developed just a few months ago. Companies developing AI models “are never going to make money”, Acemoglu said. “They are losing hundreds of billions of dollars every year.”

One may discount Altman’s new modesty as a PR feint. Somebody may have told him that equating the AI revolution with mass joblessness was not smart politics. But misgivings about AI’s vaunted capabilities are more than a marketing twist. The grand, epochal promise may be in trouble. Maybe artificial intelligence can’t deliver at a price society is willing to pay.

fullText:
The World Cup may be over, but soccer continues to draw strong viewership. A USL Championship match following the World Cup recorded the second-highest TV audience in USL history.

The Pittsburgh Riverhounds-Louisville City FC match on July 18 averaged 453,000 viewers. That is the second-highest recorded audience in USL history. The 2024 USL Championship Final averaged 606,000 viewers on CBS.

Viewership for Pittsburgh-Louisville was only slightly lower than MLS in primetime on Fox the day before. Nashville-Atlanta averaged 587,000 viewers on Fox. However, unlike the USL, MLS airs all of its games on streaming via Apple TV, meaning it’s unclear how many additional viewers watched on the streamer.

The USL, which operates below MLS in the U.S. soccer pyramid, is attempting to compete with the higher-level league. Its newest media rights deal includes over-the-air exposure on CBS and cable broadcasts on ESPN and CBS Sports Network. MLS has an over-the-air deal with Fox, but the network is not scheduled to air another MLS game until the MLS Cup.

In 2028, the USL plans to launch “USL Premier,” which would compete directly with MLS. Unlike MLS, however, USL Premier is scheduled to feature promotion and relegation from the USL Championship.

The USL Championship still has a way to go to compete with MLS fully. The 2025 MLS Cup averaged 994,000 viewers on Fox and Fox Deportes, which is more than any USL matchup on television. Viewership for the MLS Cup again does not include viewership on Apple TV.

But if this latest viewership mark is any indication, there appears to be momentum for the USL following the World Cup. If the USL wants to compete with MLS one day truly, it will need to continue building on this viewership success.

title: ‘YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!’ – Skip Bayless Accuses LeBron James of ‘Ring Chasing’ After 76ers Move

fullText:
Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.

As usual, Bayless didn’t hold back after James ended his three-week hold-up in free agency by going to a team loaded with talent.

The 76ers were reportedly not on James’ radar until they acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. Without giving up VJ Edgecombe or Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia now has a stacked core that is as good, if not better, than any NBA team.

After nearly a month of speculation, the 22-time All-Star snubbed the Miami Heat, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Cleveland Cavaliers, the other frontrunners to get his signature.

A few hours after news broke that James is now a 76er, Bayless reacted.

“CONGRATS, LEBRON! YOU MADE THE OBVIOUS RING-CHASING CHOICE! YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!” Bayless tweeted.

On Friday’s “The Skip Bayless Show,” the veteran sports journalist added more context to his message.

“This wasn’t about basketball happiness! … This was about ring chasing. What team gave LeBron James the best chance to win a fifth, maybe even a sixth championship? It was obviously from the start the Philadelphia 76ers,” Bayless said.

According to Bayless, the 41-year-old superstar wouldn’t take his talents to the Golden State Warriors, which the podcaster named the “Olden State,” if James had gone there.

Bayless continued that he didn’t predict the Timberwolves to win the James sweepstakes, as the 21-time All-NBA wouldn’t want to live in Minneapolis.

The Cavaliers offered a storybook ending, but Bayless didn’t see this version of James as the right fit on that roster.

For the former Fox Sports talk show host, the “happiness” driven decision for James would have been to take his talents back to South Beach, where he could compete for a championship and play golf “all year round.”

The allure of returning to a place where he won two championships and where Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo now lead the roster was not enough to sway James.

MORE: ‘Legacy-Wise, It Didn’t Add Up’ – LeBron James’ Former Teammate Questions NBA Legend’s $8 Million 76ers Deal

Bayless said that it was a no-brainer for James to choose Philadelphia after the 76ers pulled off what he called the “steal of the century” by getting Brown.

The analyst also argued that Maxey and VJ Edgecombe provide enviable youth and speed to surround a player entering his 24th NBA season.

Finally, there is Joel Embiid, who, when healthy, Bayless called the closest the NBA has seen to a Shaquille O’Neal.

Bayless’ criticism of James isn’t new or surprising. Over the past few years, he has been taking shots at the Akron, Ohio, native’s championships, claiming they were won by stacking his teams.

James likely knew he would be criticized regardless of which team he chose to play for. Bayless took his shots, but the only thing that matters to the 76ers’ brand-new acquisition is a chance to win championship No. 5.

fullText:
The future of Rodri has been a hot topic ever since the 2026 World Cup ended. All week Rodri has been linked with a summer move to La Liga giants, while Manchester City were hoping to extend Rodri’s contract. Now it has been reported that Real Madrid do indeed hope to sign Manchester City’s midfield general this summer. All of a sudden, a summer defining moment has landed at Manchester City’s doorstep.

David Ornstein and Mario Cortegana have reported for The Athletic that Real Madrid are aiming to sign Rodri this summer. Furthermore, it is reported that Real Madrid are confident of securing the Ballon d’Or-winning midfielder. It is also reported that as yet no direct talks have taken place between Manchester City and Real Madrid over a deal for Rodri. It is also included in The Athletic report that Manchester City are hopeful that Rodri will see out the final year of his contract. However, Rodri has previously expressed his wish to return to Spain and now Real Madrid are determined to make Rodri’s wish come true this summer.

A fork in the moment has arrived for Manchester City in the summer transfer window. David Ornstein and Mario Cortegana’s report illustrates that Real Madrid do indeed want to sign Rodri this summer. Rodri’s wish to one day play for the La Liga giants is by now well-established. City now have a decision to make assuming that Real Madrid can satisfy City’s asking price to sell the World Cup winner.

Does Manchester City hold Rodri to the final year of his contract? Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. A fully fit Rodri turns City from a very good side into an elite side. Selling Rodri would create a sizable void in Manchester City’s midfield and in their leadership. Is that something City are willing to allow to occur? That answer isn’t immediately clear but the fact that Rodri is so important to City may provide that particular answer.

The other side to the coin is whether Manchester City keeps a player who clearly wants to leave the club. Typically, besides Bernardo Silva, City do not keep players who wish to leave. This is the situation that they find themselves in with Rodri. It is no secret that Rodri wants to a move to Real Madrid. That has been obvious since the World Cup concluded. Perhaps Rodri’s time at City has naturally concluded as he has nothing left to achieve at the club. He has scaled every mountain.

Do the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders want to keep player, no matter how important they are, who doesn’t want to be there? The answer to that particular question, has the potential to massively alter City’s summer transfer window plans.

Manchester City have seemingly reached a defining moment this summer. Rodri remains Manchester City’s most important player. Real Madrid now want to sign him, and he wants a move back to Spain. Whatever City decides to do with Rodri will define their summer. It is that big, and hopefully a decision one way or another comes quickly so City can plan for what lies ahead with or without Rodri.

No team. No coach. No training facilities.

When Salote Sisifa became CEO of Tonga Netball in 2014, she had a blank canvas. Some would call it an empty cupboard.

Twelve years and much upheaval later, the Pacific Islanders are ranked eighth in the world. For context, that's just behind Wales and ahead of Scotland and Northern Ireland.

Tonga launch their first Commonwealth Games netball campaign on Saturday in Glasgow when they face Australia, the world's preeminent team.

Their story is remarkable. It tells of how TV anchor Sisifa went from reading the news to making the news, changing her country's sporting future.

It takes in national crises that include a 2022 volcanic eruption of quite staggering force, the destructive tsunami that followed, and the arrival of Covid-19 - almost two years after most of the world was first hit - to hamper relief efforts.

Sisifa said she would resign if she failed as CEO. She's still firmly at the helm.

Tonga consists of more than 170 islands and is located in the South Pacific.

It is about 2,600 miles from Melbourne, Australia, and its population of 105,000 could almost squeeze into the stands of the famous Melbourne Cricket Ground.

The islands are home to a national netball team who have nailed down a top 10 world ranking for the past four years, but it took a meteoric rise to reach this position.

Sisifa and head coach Jaqua Pori-Makea-Simpson have travelled thousands of miles to recruit players, securing their star shooter thanks to a persuasive grandma.

They still face challenges, with their pathway side - below the senior national squad - having to train in a bank's car park.

When Sisifa signed up, she found netball in Tonga was little more than a social game.

She swiftly committed Tonga to entering a team for the 2015 Pacific Games.

"The scores... we were being beaten like it was a cricket match," she recalls.

More like rugby scorelines perhaps - Tonga lost 88-21 to Samoa, and 81-27 to Papua New Guinea.

Sisifa went to the national governing body for netball in Tonga and said: "Please give me five years. We're going to make some dramatic changes. If it doesn't work within the five years, I would happily resign."

The national body backed Sisifa, so she got to work.

She needed a coach with international pedigree and so wrote to eight candidates. Only one replied.

New Zealand-born Pori-Makea-Simpson joined in 2019.

Sisifa remembers their frank first conversation: "We had no dollar sign to our name. I said if that's what you're looking for, Team Tonga is not the place."

Then came mention of Tonga's vision.

"I said, by 2025, I want Tonga to make top 10 in the world," Sisifa told BBC World Service.

Pori-Makea-Simpson recalls: "I went... you're mad. That is obscene, and I'm not sure you understand what the netball world looks like."

Players with Tongan backgrounds were sought, even if they had never visited the country. This led to some backlash, but Pori-Makea-Simpson felt the players she found shared a culture with islanders.

"Taking them back to Tonga and watching them thrive and grow with their people, it's been beautiful," she said.

The spirit of Tala: The rapid rise of Tonga's netball team

Uneeq Palavi, also known as Pav, has a Samoan mother and Tongan father. She grew up in Australia and has been a Melbourne Mavericks fan favourite.

In 2019, she initially ignored Tonga's call, not feeling ready.

Sisifa roped in Palavi's Tongan grandmother to apply a little persuasion. It worked.

Tonga won silver at the Pacific Games and jumped from 42nd to 19th in the world.

They were moving in the right direction, but then came problem upon problem: a volcanic eruption, tsunami and pandemic lockdown all struck in early 2022.

When the underwater Hunga-Tonga Hunga-Haʻapai erupted, it resulted in the biggest atmospheric explosion recorded by modern instrumentation.

Nasa said it was hundreds of times more powerful than the atomic bomb the US dropped on Hiroshima in 1945.

Four people in Tonga died, and devastation from the eruption and subsequent tsunami was vast. For a while, communication with the island was difficult.

Pori-Makea-Simpson, who was out of the country, had to lead without Tonga Netball's support.

"I had no team, no administration, I didn't have uniforms, I had no equipment," she says.

She had an upcoming PacificAus Sports series and had to draw together a squad almost from scratch, searching social media for eligible players.

Most had never met before they gathered at Sydney Airport five days before competition began.

"I didn't even know their names. They didn't know each other's names. Even when we had finished the tournament, I still didn't know everybody's surnames," Pori-Makea-Simpson recalls.

Against the odds, Tonga won gold.

Star shooter Palavi speaks of a cultural bond.

"Playing for Tonga is always like playing with 15 of my other sisters," she said.

Next came a rare World Cup appearance in 2023, with the team taking on the nickname of Tala - a rare bird that is a symbol of hope.

They finished eighth in South Africa and now comes a Commonwealth Games debut.

Team spirit, and considerable talent, have taken this team a long way.

"I think non-Pacific Island people would call it a camaraderie. It's not a camaraderie. It's an innate spirituality that connects them," says coach Pori-Makea-Simpson.

"In a way that is very, very hard to understand from the outside. You can feel it from the people in the crowd.

"Irrespective of what happens to us in terms of scoreboard, their pride and gratitude to us wearing their crest and their flag will never falter.

"And they're not proud of us because we're winning. They're proud of us because we're Tongan. I am probably the proudest non-Tongan walking on the planet."

title: Joshua v Prenga - heavyweight predictions
description: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's heavyweight fight between Anthony Joshua and Kristian Prenga.
fullText:
Anthony Joshua returns to the ring on Saturday against the relatively unknown Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, knowing that victory would set up a long-awaited showdown with Tyson Fury.

Joshua, a two-time world champion and Olympic gold medallist, has won 29 fights - 26 by stoppage - and lost four.

Albanian Prenga enters the fight with an impressive record of his own, having achieved all of his 20 victories with stoppages while suffering only one defeat.

However, the 35-year-old has never faced anyone close to Joshua's level.

Joshua v Prenga - all you need to know

After Fury comfortably dispatched Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday, can Joshua can come through his own warm-up bout?

This will be Joshua's first fight since he was involved in a car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of two close friends, Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

The Fury-Joshua fight has been a decade in the making. Contracts have been signed, with the blockbuster bout expected to take place later this year.

But could Prenga spoil the party and pull off a huge shock to go down in boxing history as the man who got in the way of Joshua-Fury happening?

Radio commentary from Jeddah will begin from about 20:30 BST on BBC Radio 5 Live, BBC Sounds, and the BBC Sport website and app.

Live text commentary will begin at 19:30 on the BBC Sport website and app.

BBC Sport spoke to figures from the boxing world to get their predictions for Saturday's fight.

"I think AJ will win by a stoppage late. He has to be careful at the beginning of the fight because a lot of Prenga's stoppages have come in the first couple of rounds - he rarely goes past six rounds, so that's uncharted territory."

"I think AJ will have a look in the first round but it will be over round three or four. I think he'll go right though this guy. I hope he does and we see him and Fury."

Ready to 'conquer Earth' - Joshua embraces comeback spotlight

Joshua v Prenga - all you need to know

"Joshua coming back from what he has is a testament to himself. His attitude and mental resilience. I haven't seen much of Prenga, but I've heard he's a tough guy. If the right Anthony Joshua goes out there and performs, he's a hard night for anyone. If he goes out and performs, he can put anyone on their back. He needs to not overthink. Do your job, get in and get out."

"Obviously it's been an incredibly difficult time for AJ but he seems mentally and physically in a good place, training under Team Usyk.

"I expect him to go out there and emphatically deal with Prenga, who has not fought at anywhere near Joshua's level. So Joshua to win within the first four rounds."

"I think it's a fascinating opponent for AJ to take, because although you may criticise Prenga's style and that it might not look the best, he was a tough unbeaten kickboxer. We saw with Rico Verhoeven against Usyk that these kickboxers can make it tough. I expect AJ to look fresh, establish a quick jab early and have attention to detail.

"He looks very lean, I think he'll be quicker than before and I think he's going to get a clean win. Prenga will try but I think AJ will walk him on to a shot."

"In recent times, you're never quite sure which version of Joshua would turn up on the night.

"But saying that, any version of Joshua will have too much for Prenga. He's big and powerful, but I think he's out of his depth.

"I think Joshua will be a little bit more confident and forceful against this level of opposition. I think it will be three or four rounds before Joshua gets to him with a stoppage."

"You will not see a third round. Joshua will win by a brutal, nasty and vicious knockout."

"I predict a brutal Joshua win, early. It won't go past three rounds. Do not blink."

"AJ will win whenever he wants - it's a run-out for him. Prenga has a flattering record, but if you look at his style, he's pretty cumbersome. Prenga will walk on to shots but AJ's class, his jab and his power punch will have a massive impact. It depends if Joshua wants a few rounds and to practise what he's been doing with his new team.

"It will last as long as Joshua wants it to - maybe four or five rounds."

"AJ will win by knockout between rounds three and five."

"Like most, I'll be honest, I've not seen much of Prenga, but what I have seen, it's a gigantic step up.

"The last 12 to 18 months outside the ring and in with the Dubois defeat being a bad one, Joshua can be excused for this type of opponent.

"With AJ and the power he carries, it could be over in a matter of seconds. I expect him to take his time a little bit and for him to knock Prenga out in three rounds."

title: USA's Lyles wins 100m in world-leading 9.79 seconds
description: Noah Lyles runs a world-leading 9.79 seconds as he claims an impressive victory in the 100m at the US athletics championships.
fullText:
Noah Lyles ran a world-leading 9.79 seconds as he claimed an impressive victory in the 100m at the US athletics championships.

He also equalled his personal best, which he set in winning gold at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, with the run at the Icahn Stadium in New York City.

The previous best 100m in 2026 was the 9.82 set by Jamaica's Oblique Seville in June.

"I think I made that 'I'm still the world's fastest man' statement," said Lyles.

The 29-year-old American finished ahead of Ronnie Baker in second and third-placed Kenny Bednarek, who were both given a time of 9.88, while former world champion Christian Coleman was fourth in 9.93.

"Just because it is an off year doesn't mean that I plan to run slow," added Lyles, referring to there being no Olympics or World Championships this year.

"This is me being me and being me is dominant, being consistent."

Sha'Carri Richardson, the 2023 world champion, won the women's 100m as she clocked 10.77.

The 26-year-old equalled her best time of the season as Kayla White finished second with 10.90 and Tamari Davis third in 11.00.

"It just feels phenomenal to be back in a better place, just healthy mentally, physically and emotionally," said Richardson, who has had troubles off the track.

"Everything me and coach have been working on, it's starting to show consistently."

fullText:
Defending World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC when they meet the New York Mets on Sunday.

The Dodgers lead the National League again in 2026, with last season's Most Valuable Player, Shohei Ohtani, to the fore as they target a third consecutive World Series title.

The struggling Mets are in need of inspiration from star man Juan Soto as they look to turn around a difficult start to the season.

The game sets up a run of 10 consecutive live Sunday night MLB matches on the BBC, including the season finale on September 27 before four post-season games the following week.

Why Dodgers are on brink of World Series dynasty

The night the Tartan Army took over iconic Fenway Park

The Dodgers' record of 65 wins and 38 defeats means they are likely to win the National League West for the 13th time in 14th years.

Their recent dominance is built around Ohtani, whose achievements are now compared to the greatest players in the history of the game.

His ability to both hit and pitch at the top level consistently - he already has 22 home runs this year and has recorded eight wins as a pitcher - demonstrates a similar skill-set to the legendary two-way player Babe Ruth.

Ohtani has been named Most Valuable Player in his league four times, including last season, when the Dodgers became the first franchise in 25 years to win consecutive World Series titles.

Dominican left-fielder Soto became the highest-paid player in baseball history in 2024 when he left the New York Yankees and signed a $765m deal with their bitter cross-city rivals the Mets.

He hit his 250th career home run against the Yankees earlier this season, one of 21 home runs he has delivered in 2026.

Despite Soto's contribution, the Mets narrowly missed out on a post-season berth last year and now sit bottom of the National League East with 43 wins to 60 defeats.

title: Sinner, Djokovic withdraw from Montreal Masters
description: Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic have pulled out of next month's ATP Montreal Masters, organizers Tennis Canada said Friday.In a packed schedule, world number one Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic both had deep runs at Wimbledon earlier this month, where Italian Sinner won the men's title and Serbian Djokovic reached the semi-finals.
fullText:
Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic have pulled out of next month's ATP Montreal Masters, organizers Tennis Canada said Friday.

In a packed schedule, world number one Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic both had deep runs at Wimbledon earlier this month, where Italian Sinner won the men's title and Serbian Djokovic reached the semi-finals.

"After carefully considering all the factors together with my team, we have made the difficult decision to withdraw from Montreal," Sinner said in a statement.

"It is never easy to miss such an important event, but we believe this is the right decision to prioritize my health."

The Montreal men's event, which takes place August 1-13, is an ATP Masters 1000 tournament, and a key pre-US Open stopping point.

The parallel women's WTA 1000 tournament takes place this year in Toronto, with the two competitions switching between the cities on alternate years.

Organizers expressed disappointment at the last-minute withdrawals, noting that the two men also pulled out of last year's event in Toronto.

"We respect their decisions and understand that, with such a demanding schedule, players' health must remain the priority," tournament director Valerie Tetreault said in a statement.

"That said, we believe the frequency of these last-minute withdrawals in the last few years raises a broader issue for our sport."

"Masters 1000 events are among the flagship tournaments on the tour, and fans rightfully expect to see the world's best compete."

Tetreault said organizers are in discussions with the ATP over "adjustments" that are "needed in the near future to better protect the integrity of our Masters 1000 events while remaining mindful of the realities players face."

World number two Alexander Zverev -- this year's French Open champion and Wimbledon finalist -- is now expected to be the Montreal top seed, followed by Quebec native Felix Auger-Aliassime.

Third-ranked Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz had already withdrawn from Montreal over a lingering wrist injury.

He is targeting a return at the Cincinnati ATP Masters 1000 tournament, which begins immediately after Montreal.

The US Open, the year's final Grand Slam, starts on August 30 in New York.

title: Meet SLB: The $70 billion oil services giant poised to cash in on AI data centers and the post-Strait of Hormuz oil exploration boom
description: For nearly a century, SLB has helped energy companies find hard-to-reach reserves. Now the global energy realignment is giving the French-Texan company a fresh growth story.
fullText:
In 1912, the French physicist Conrad Schlumberger could be found kneeling on the ground of his family's estate in Normandy, strategically placing wired electrodes in the soil. He was performing conductivity tests to detect the buried ruins of a medieval abbey destroyed there during the French Revolution. But the experiment had a broader purpose: proving that electric instruments could be used to reveal and map underground structures from the surface. Schlumberger's approach worked, and it turned out to be a remarkably effective tool for a more lucrative enterprise: finding oil.

Conrad and his brother Marcel Schlumberger went on to create the first well logs—using electric cables for subsurface readings, producing outputs that resembled EKG heart monitor readings. The method became the backbone of modern geophysical prospecting, and supercharged the growth of a burgeoning oil and gas exploration industry worldwide. In 1926 the brothers founded the Société de Prospection Électrique (Electric Prospecting Co.). That company—eventually Schlumberger and now SLB—rapidly expanded into Venezuela, the United States, and the Soviet Union. By the end of the 1930s, Schlumberger had moved into the Middle East, more than 20 years before the formation of OPEC.

Over a century of upheaval and industrial reinvention, SLB has grown into the largest oilfield services and energy technology company in the world. Known in the industry as "Big Blue" for its signature blue uniforms, it has remained in all those key locations, and expanded to another 100 countries.

Now, as the Middle East's oil and gas sector rebounds from the biggest energy supply shock in modern history—the monthslong closure of the Strait of Hormuz—and Venezuela rebuilds its energy infrastructure, SLB is ideally positioned to profit from this growth in its next century.

In the energy services industry, which does all the grunt work for oil producers—drilling, fracking, and, increasingly, digital and AI-driven automation services—SLB is larger than its better-known American rivals, Halliburton and Baker Hughes. With 109,000 workers worldwide, SLB employs more people than ExxonMobil and Chevron combined.

In Venezuela, SLB and Chevron—two companies that never left the country even after the Hugo Chávez regime expropriated oil assets—will work with state-owned PDVSA to reinvigorate the world's largest proven oil reserves. In the Middle East, SLB partners with Saudi Aramco, the United Arab Emirates' ADNOC, Kuwait Petroleum, and others.
