title: Opinion - Ukraine may already be winning World War III for an oblivious West
description: Ukraine is now dealing the decisive blow that may win the global war that much of the Western world still fails to recognize is being waged against it.
fullText:
Against all odds, Ukraine is right on the point of winning World War III.

In July 2022, we argued that Russian President Vladimir Putin had blundered his way into a dystopian global conflict that pitted Russia, China and their Axis of Evil allies — Iran and North Korea — against the West by invading Ukraine.

Despite our warnings, Washington and Brussels in 2023 continued to act as if Putin's war was merely an Eastern European conflict. They failed to grasp that Russia's aggression against Ukraine was the same threat as Chinese President Xi Jinping aggression against Taiwan and the Philippines.

In February 2023, China was actively conducting live-fire drills around Taiwan by sea and air. North Korea was aggressively conducting missile tests over the Sea of Japan. Iran was rapidly expanding its nuclear weapons program, and at the time had amassed 154 pounds of  highly enriched uranium, enough to build "several nuclear weapons," according to Rafael Grossi, the director of the International Atomic Energy Agency. After watching then-President Joe Biden's State of the Union speech that month, we wondered whether he wasn't already late to World War III.

Yet it was crickets at the White House in terms of connecting the dots between Putin and Xi's escalating war against the West. Biden's mantra was that Ukraine is an isolated conflict, and that it was only a question of defending Kyiv for as long as it takes. There was no talk then of defending U.S. allies and global interests from Putin and Xi's aim to create and wield a new world order. Nor did Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks and atrocities against Israeli civilians on Oct. 7, 2023 make it clear to Team Biden that the risk to global security had expanded far beyond the front lines in Ukraine.

It seemed Putin and Xi's visions of a new multi-polar order were openly clashing with traditional Western-style liberal democracy that had largely ensured global peace since the end of World War II in 1945. And the bad guys were winning.

Only one country fully understood what was at stake on a global basis: That was Ukraine, of course. By merely resisting and refusing to capitulate to Putin, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and his generals were holding back a tide of global setbacks for the West.

But now things have changed. Ukraine, chiefly on its own, using a wide assortment of asymmetrical kinetic means, is no longer fighting a long, losing defensive battle. Rather, it is dealing the decisive blow that may help to win the global war that much of the Western world still fails to recognize is being waged against it.

Zelensky has always understood the threat. Days before Putin invaded Ukraine, he warned that Europe and the world were facing their "biggest security crisis since the Cold War."

The Ukrainian president reiterated this just months ago, on the fourth anniversary of the start of the war. Zelensky said that Putin "has already started World War Three." Zelensky added that he believes "stopping Putin today and preventing him from occupying Ukraine is a victory for the whole world."

Over time Ukraine, has held Russia back. Its armed forces have repeatedly repelled spring and summer ground offensives, inflicting more than 1.4 million Russian casualties.

Today, with its strategic drone campaign, Kyiv is decimating Russia's oil and gas industry. It has now hit all 11 of the country's largest refineries, including a facility as far away as Siberia. It is estimated that Ukraine has destroyed or degraded as much as 43 percent of Russia's total refining capacity, causing $13.5 billion in direct losses to its already stressed war economy. Widespread shortages now persist throughout Russia — the situation is especially dire in Russian-occupied Crimea, whose isolation is nearly complete.

Ukraine is also decimating Russia's domestic supply chain. Beginning last week, Kyiv started striking the distribution centers of WildBerries, Moscow's version of Amazon. Damage is already in the billions. Ukraine claims that the company is playing an essential in equipping Russian soldiers — both those currently in the field and those about to be mobilized.

Beyond Eastern Europe, Ukraine's success is forcing Russia to retrench, especially in the Middle East. Putin was already unable to come to the aid of now-ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad. Even Iran, a wartime ally against Ukraine, is also beyond his help under the weight of U.S. attacks.

In addition, Russian paramilitary forces are under heavy attack by Islamic State terrorists across the Sahel in Sub-Saharan Africa, especially in Mali. Putin also lost his foothold in Venezuela and is in danger of losing Cuba to the U.S.

Perhaps most significantly, Ukraine has forced China to hedge its bets. In 2025, Beijing became Kyiv's largest trading partner as the two countries' bilateral trade hit $21 billion. Yet even so, China is still paying a price for Ukraine's success. Kyiv's revolutionary innovations in the area of drone warfare are forcing Xi to recalibrate and even rethink any plans to invade Taiwan.

Even North Korea is reeling. Its soldiers for sale have died in Ukraine and its artillery and munitions have been proven marginal.

Putin, once seen as a hedge against Xi's domination of Southeast Asia, is now only a weakened junior partner to Beijing. Need evidence? Xi has rejected Putin's hopes of a Siberia 2 gas pipeline to generate badly needed revenue. Beijing has reportedly told Moscow to "stop raising the subject altogether." So much for their much-vaunted "no-limits partnership."

World War III is not yet won. But Ukraine is putting victory in the West's grasp — if only Washington and Brussels will seize it.

Mark Toth writes on national security and foreign policy. Col. (Ret.) Jonathan Sweet served 30 years as a military intelligence officer and led the U.S. European Command Intelligence Engagement Division from 2012 to 2014. They are the cofounders of INTREP360 and the INTREP360 Intelligence Report on Substack.

title: Kelly and Agyarko ooze confidence before title bout
description: With the IBF world light-middleweight title in his possession, Josh Kelly feels "it's a different version of me" since he dethroned Bakhram Murtazaliev and promises to "put on a show" in his maiden defence against Caoimhin Agyarko on Saturday.
fullText:
Briton Josh Kelly says we will see a "different version" of him when he makes the first defence of his IBF light-middleweight title against Caoimhin Agyarko on Saturday.

Kelly rebuilt from his sole career loss in 2021 to beat Bakhram Murtazaliev and claim the title in January, winning the belt in his 20th professional bout.

Belfast's Agyarko has also overcome adversity to earn a seat at world title level, having been cut by promoter Matchroom after what was then a career-best win over Troy Williamson in 2023.

Both men will walk to the ring in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's heavyweight return against Kristian Prenga fully aware of how tough it has been to get to this stage.

"Being a world champion does something to you," Kelly said at Thursday's final news conference.

"I thought it was a myth beforehand but how I'm going about my work in the gym is just different. It's a different version of me.

"When I have that confidence, it's a hard night for anyone: 'Boots' [Jaron Ennis], [Sebastian] Fundora - any of them.

"I'm going to come in on Saturday, show there's levels to this game and put on a show."

Adversity to history - Agyarko's world title dream

The two days which could make or break Fury-Joshua

Ready to 'conquer Earth' - Joshua embraces comeback spotlight

Kelly's fast start against Murtazaliev was the platform for his title success as he mixed movement with measured attacks.

Although just nine of his 18 wins have come inside the distance, he felt the big-punching defending champion "was feeling the shots" and reluctant to open up.

The Sunderland fighter is promising a similar performance and "it will be early on" when he breaks Agyarko's spirit, but the challenger has scoffed at that notion.

Undefeated in 18 contests - seven inside the distance - Agyarko had to dig deep to come through his last outing against Ishmael Davis.

Agyarko was knocked down in the 12th round but made it to the final bell with his right eye swollen shut and had ultimately done enough to win by split-decision.

The 29-year-old suffered damage to his left eye in the previous contest, a points win over Ryan Kelly, so he will know he can ill-afford to become a stationary target for the champion.

Agyarko and Kelly both appeared agitated during Thursday's news conference and there was a heated exchange when they faced off.

'Black Thunder' rejected claims that he will wilt in the early stages of the contest and promised a career-best performance.

"He's a world champion and a good fighter, but this nonsense I will lose confidence early - I've heard it all before," Agyarko said.

"It's my time to go and prove everybody wrong, just as I have the last three or four fights when I've been the underdog and the 'B side' but have always come out on top.

"I'm prepared for the best Josh Kelly and you're going to see the best Caoimhin Agyarko so it will be a great fight, but I believe I will create history.

"I will run through brick walls to become the first black Irish world champion and if I have to beat the best Josh Kelly, then so be it."

title: Rodri to have back surgery but Maresca brushes off transfer speculation
description: World Cup winner Rodri is to have back surgery, says new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca.
fullText:
World Cup winner Rodri will have surgery on a back issue on Monday, new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The 30-year-old Spain captain guided his country to World Cup glory last week and was named the Golden Ball winner as player of the tournament.

But the midfielder's last two seasons at club level were heavily disrupted - an anterior cruciate ligament injury leaving him sidelined for the majority of the 2024-25 campaign before several setbacks last season meant he was often unavailable.

The Ballon d'Or winner was back to his best at the World Cup but, speaking at his first news conference since being appointed City boss, Maresca said Rodri now needs surgery followed by recuperation.

"Now, [he has] surgery on Monday. Then he needs a holiday, he needs to rest and recover and then he will be back with us," the Italian coach said.

Maresca did not elaborate on when Rodri might return though he did dismiss speculation around the Spaniard's future at Etihad Stadium following reports in the past week linking him with a move to Real Madrid.

"Around big players there are always speculations so I am not worried about that," he said.

"I think it is normal, also because they [Spain] won the World Cup and because he is one of the best players. I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he is a top player."

Of other players still to return, Maresca said he expected to have them in the squad three or four days before City face Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday, 16 August.

Why Maresca? What Man City fans can expect from Guardiola's successor

Rodri's stock at all-time high as he adds to trophy collection

In his first news conference since succeeding Pep Guardiola last month, Maresca found himself fielding questions about the Catalan, who won 20 trophies in his 10 years at the club.

The 46-year-old knows only too well the tough act he has to follow having worked as Guardiola's assistant during the 2022-23 Treble-winning season.

"I want to say it is a privilege because it's the reason why the club decided to go for me, that is a privilege," he said.

"I have said many times, I consider Pep the best coach in the world in the last 20-25 years. It is a challenge [to replace him]."

Maresca, who called time on his time at Chelsea in January after 18 months, acknowledged the challenge of arriving at a club who have had just three managers in 16 years.

"That is not normal and has not happened often," he said. "I am confident that we can continue to do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last 14, 15 years since Roberto Mancini was here.

"I know the organisation quite well and the people inside the club from years ago. The structure understands to give time for everything.

"Since Manchester City contacted me, I had no doubt about joining this fantastic club."

Maresca hinted that there were "a few things to do" in the transfer window but would not be drawn on the futures of players including goalkeeper James Trafford, who has been linked with a move away from the club, and returning midfielder Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Everton but is back in training with City.

title: LA Dodgers and MVP Ohtani launch summer of live baseball on BBC
description: World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC.
fullText:
Defending World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC when they meet the New York Mets on Sunday.

The Dodgers lead the National League again in 2026, with last season's Most Valuable Player, Shohei Ohtani, to the fore as they target a third consecutive World Series title.

The struggling Mets are in need of inspiration from star man Juan Soto as they look to turn around a difficult start to the season.

The game sets up a run of 10 consecutive live Sunday night MLB matches on the BBC, including the season finale on September 27 before four post-season games the following week.

Why Dodgers are on brink of World Series dynasty

The night the Tartan Army took over iconic Fenway Park

The Dodgers' record of 65 wins and 38 defeats means they are likely to win the National League West for the 13th time in 14th years.

Their recent dominance is built around Ohtani, whose achievements are now compared to the greatest players in the history of the game.

His ability to both hit and pitch at the top level consistently - he already has 22 home runs this year and has recorded eight wins as a pitcher - demonstrates a similar skill-set to the legendary two-way player Babe Ruth.

Ohtani has been named Most Valuable Player in his league four times, including last season, when the Dodgers became the first franchise in 25 years to win consecutive World Series titles.

Dominican left-fielder Soto became the highest-paid player in baseball history in 2024 when he left the New York Yankees and signed a $765m deal with their bitter cross-city rivals the Mets.

He hit his 250th career home run against the Yankees earlier this season, one of 21 home runs he has delivered in 2026.

Despite Soto's contribution, the Mets narrowly missed out on a post-season berth last year and now sit bottom of the National League East with 43 wins to 60 defeats.

This season, the MLB Bases Covered Live team will again be led by play-by-play announcer Melanie Newman, with former St Louis Cardinals first baseman Xavier Scruggs and Maccabees guitarist Felix White alongside to call the action for seasoned baseball fans and new viewers.

During the 2026 Fifa World Cup, baseball played an unexpectedly large role in the experiences of football fans and players from the UK as they enjoyed memorable outings to ballparks across the US.

After defeating Haiti in their opening game in nearby Foxborough, Scotland's Tartan Army took over Fenway Park in Boston to celebrate while watching the Red Sox take on the Texas Rangers.

title: Tyler Adams Explains Mauricio Pochettino’s Impact on USMNT
description: We discuss the World Cup awards and whether the right players received them.
fullText:
The biggest news that fans of the United States Men’s National Team are waiting for is the decision by current head coach Mauricio Pochettino. Will he accept the contract extension that U.S. Soccer offered before the start of the World Cup? That’s the question that U.S. Soccer hopes will be answered soon.

Midfielder Tyler Adams spoke with Stars & Stripes FC this week as part of his work with Allstate opening up a mini-pitch in Atlanta. He took the time during that interview to explain the impact Pochettino had on him and the rest of the USMNT.

“I’ve been very fortunate with the managers I’ve been able to work under and learn from. [How] Pochettino leads a group of people and the culture he leads with is so important,” Adams said. “Put the tactics and how he improved me as a player aside, how he improved me as a person, the intangibles and the culture he created was incredible.”

Pochettino led the USMNT to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, setting a record for most USMNT wins at a single World Cup in the process. Since he took over as head coach in September 2024, he has a 17W-12L-2D record. During the World Cup, he had the team competing at their highest ability until it all fell apart in the Round of 16 against Belgium. Still, having a full cycle of Pochettino, despite the history with coaches getting a second cycle, could bring some continuity that the team hasn’t had in quite some time.

Pochettino has said that a decision on his future will come soon. Should he continue as coach, it seems like he will have a player pool that will fight for him as they attempt to build on the foundation they’ve set and keep fans engaged and supportive. World Cup qualifying begins next fall, but they have Concacaf Nations League as well as the 2027 Gold Cup before that. Pochettino’s decision will affect the team’s approach to those competitions.

title: Devlin opens up on 'too stressful' Hearts exit for Rangers
description: Cammy Devlin says it was "too stressful" to head to the World Cup with his club future still to be decided - although the extra time taken did lead to a move to Rangers.
fullText:
Cammy Devlin says it was "too stressful" to head to the World Cup with his club future still to be decided, although the extra time taken did lead to a move to Rangers "that was too good to pass up".

The 28-year-old midfielder's contract was running down as he joined the Australia squad just three days after being "devastated" by the final-day loss to Celtic that meant Heart of Midlothian were pipped to the Scottish title by their hosts.

Devlin was weighing up whether to accept a new deal from the Edinburgh club amid rival interest, before Derek McInnes' own switch from Hearts to become Rangers manager decided the midfielder's destiny.

"The game was on the Saturday and I flew out to the World Cup on the Tuesday," Devlin said in his first public interview since joining the Glasgow club.

Rangers buy Serbia's Dragojevic from Partizan

Pandur joined Rangers after Hull planned new number one

Devlin sees McInnes relationship bloom already for Rangers

"It was devastating, but I didn't have much time to reflect on how last season ended and then straight into the World Cup, which is one of the most special moments of your career.

"My mum, my dad and my girlfriend are over in America supporting you. So you are trying to enjoy that as much as you can.

"I thought it would be a good idea going there off-contract, but it wasn't.

"It was too stressful. It was hard just being in the moment being at the World Cup and dealing with all that and the noise around it, and my dad asking me every day what's going on."

Devlin failed to add to his five Australia caps at the World Cup and a week after their last-32 defeat by Egypt, Hearts announced he would not be signing a new contract, with Rangers announcing his capture the following day.

McInnes had gone from a position of trying to persuade Devlin to stay at Tynecastle one week to one of enticing the midfielder to Ibrox the next.

"Everyone knows the relationship I have with the gaffer where we are super close and he was so good for me at Hearts and everyone knows the season we had there," Devlin said. "He helped me so much as a player.

"I was not trying to focus on it too much and just enjoy the World Cup, but when the opportunity came, it was one that was too good to pass up."

Devlin says it was "a hard decision to make" to leave Hearts.

"Hearts is such a special football club and I will be forever grateful for giving me the opportunity to play football outside Australia," he said.

"There were obviously other things I had to weigh up with Hearts - I've never been in that position where I've been off-contract.

"Rangers was one that came a bit later and I've been in Scotland for quite a while now and know how big a football club it is.

"Being a Rangers player is super special and something I never thought would happen. It was just something I couldn't say no to."

As for last season's title heartache, Devlin added: "Football is cruel sometimes and you just have to pick yourself up and take the next opportunity.

"Hopefully I can go one better with Rangers."

title: Scotland's Gunn concedes four in San Jose debut defeat

fullText:
Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn suffered a nightmare debut for San Jose Earthquakes as they slumped to a 4-0 defeat at home to Orlando City in their first match following Major League Soccer's break for the World Cup.

It was the 30-year-old's first game since his national side failed to qualify for the knockout stages following a 3-0 loss to Brazil in their final group game - and his first club game since coming on as a substitute in Nottingham Forest's 1-1 Premier League draw with Crystal Palace in February.

But, in truth, Gunn could take little blame for any of the goals while also producing a couple of saves that prevented a more painful loss for Bruce Arena's hosts.

Visiting centre-half David Brekalo was left unmarked as he headed home Eduard Atuesta's free-kick with just seven minutes gone.

Winger Ivan Angulo doubled City's lead in the 29th minute with a powerful low drive into the far corner from just outside the penalty box.

France legend Antoine Griezmann marked his debut following the 35-year-old forward's move from Atletico Madrid by firing home from just inside the box three minutes after the break as Gunn was left exposed by a loss of possession.

Paraguay midfielder Braian Ojeda completed the rout in the 73rd minute as his header squeezed between Gunn and the near post from another Atuesta set piece.

At the other end, Gunn's opposite number, Canada's Maxime Crepeau, produced several fine saves, a couple denying Timo Werner a scoring debut for San Jose after the Germany striker's move from RB Leipzig.

title: England amputee team's World Cup dream on hold
description: Former head coach Scott Rogers has said it is "criminal" that England men's amputee football team could miss the 2026 World Cup due to a lack of funding.
fullText:
England's men's amputee football team could miss the upcoming World Cup in Mexico because of a lack of funding - a prospect the team's former head coach Scott Rogers called "criminal".

The team, who are the reigning Nations League champions, have set a GoFundMe target of £50,000 to attend November's tournament.

"I see how hard they [the players] work, I see how hard the staff work, I see the sacrifices they make and the families make as well," Rogers told BBC Breakfast.

"To get to this point now and not be able to go potentially, it's criminal really."

The Football Association funds other para national teams, but funding for the amputee programme was cut in 2006.

The England Amputee Football Association has since set up as a charity and it relies on donations and volunteers to support its men's and women's teams, along with a junior pathway.

FA representatives shadowed the men's amputee team at the 2022 World Cup and subsequently made a funding offer, but it fell short of what they felt was needed.

"Our funding model is we come on the television and people donate, and we are so grateful for that - we would love to be able to thank everyone individually for that - but it's not a funding model that is sustainable," Rogers added.

"We have a good relationship with the FA, but the problem is at the moment the information that we are getting back from them is there isn't the funding available to be able to bring amputee football under the FA's umbrella."

In the 2024-25 season, the FA generated a total turnover of £516m with an operating profit of £6m.

Meanwhile, England's men's team earned £21.5m in prize money for finishing third in this summer's World Cup.

"It's crazy. We're kind of battling against the system," said goalkeeper Thomas Atkinson.

"A lot of the teams we are competing against are full-time professionals, they are getting paid daily by clubs and the governing body, their national team fully supports them in everything they do.

"We're definitely not one of those teams."

The team have currently raised £32,427 of their £50,000 goal.

"We're playing as a hobby in a sense. We're having to pay to play whereas they're getting paid to play," Atkinson added.

"I'm not even asking to get paid to play football, I just think we as an organisation, as England – one of the biggest countries in football – shouldn't be having our national team players having to pay to attend tournaments. It's crazy, isn't it?"

An FA spokesperson said: "The England amputee team is currently independent from the FA.

"We continue to work closely with the England Amputee Football Association to support, identify and help deliver their key priorities over the coming season, and the continued development of amputee football in England."

title: Opetaia sues IBF to return cruiserweight world title
description: Boxer Jai Opetaia starts legal action in the United States to try to force the IBF to hand back the cruiserweight world title.
fullText:
Boxer Jai Opetaia has started legal action in the United States to force the IBF to hand back the cruiserweight world title.

The Australian claims the sanctioning body acted unlawfully when it stripped him of his belt following his first fight with promotional outfit Zuffa Boxing.

Opetaia filed a lawsuit in the US District Court for the District of Nevada seeking to have his title reinstated, recover damages and legal costs, and prevent the IBF from naming another cruiserweight champion while the litigation continues.

The IBF declined to comment, with a spokesperson telling BBC Sport: "We will release a statement when it is appropriate."

The 19-page complaint - obtained by BBC Sport - claims rival governing bodies have discouraged champions from facing him, citing David Benavidez's decision not to pursue a fight after Opetaia was stripped and alleging the WBC threatened to strip Noel Mikaelian if he agreed to face the Australian instead.

"The conspirators and, most recently, the WBC have taken steps to freeze out Jai from other future bouts," the lawsuit says.

The complaint also names representatives from sanction bodies the WBC, WBA and WBO - BBC Sport has contacted them for comment.

Opetaia stripped of IBF title over Zuffa belt bout

What is Zuffa Boxing and can it shake up the sport?

The case centres on the fallout from 31-year-old Opetaia's decision to sign with Zuffa Boxing, the new promotion launched by UFC president Dana White and Saudi Arabian-owned Sela and American company TKO.

Opetaia's first fight under the promotion came against Brandon Glanton in Las Vegas in March. His IBF world title was due to be defended on the same night that Zuffa Boxing introduced its inaugural cruiserweight championship belt.

According to the complaint, the IBF initially approved those arrangements, accepted a $73,000 (£54,000) sanctioning fee and appointed an official to oversee the contest, before withdrawing its sanctioning less than 48 hours before fight night.

The lawsuit argues the IBF later treated the contest as a title unification because a Zuffa Boxing belt was also being contested.

Opetaia disputes that interpretation, arguing the organisation had already accepted the Zuffa belt was merely a "trophy or token of recognition", rather than the championship of another sanctioning body. He says there was no legitimate basis for the IBF to reverse its position.

The filing says Opetaia was "placed in an impossible position" by the late decision, forcing him to choose between withdrawing from a contest he had spent months preparing for and losing "his seven-figure compensation", or proceeding with the fight and "risk being stripped of his championship".

Opetaia chose to box, defeating Glanton by unanimous decision, before the IBF subsequently vacated his title.

The lawsuit further alleges the IBF's actions were "the product of coordinated, industry-wide collusion designed to penalise Jai for signing with Zuffa Boxing and to deter other athletes from doing the same".

There is precedent of a fighter being reinstated as a world champion following legal action.

In 2004, the WBC was forced into liquidation after losing a £17m legal battle against former champion Graciano Rocchigiani.

Rocchigiani won the WBC's vacant light-heavyweight title in March 1998 after it had been relinquished by Roy Jones Jr.

But Jones decided he wanted to keep the belt and the WBC reinstated him as champion in June 1998.

In addition to the compensation, the WBC was ordered to recognise Rocchigiani as champion from 1998-2000.

Zuffa Boxing launched in June 2025 with ambitions of challenging the established promoters and sanctioning bodies that dominate the sport.

The promotion currently recognises eight weight divisions, with one Zuffa champion crowned in each category.

White has previously stated that Zuffa Boxing will not rely on the traditional world titles awarded by the WBA, WBA, WBO and IBF.

White has also expressed his desire to make changes to Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act, the 2000 US law introduced to protect boxers' rights and prevent conflicts of interest and monopolistic practices within the sport.

Changes to the legislation could potentially allow a Zuffa championship belt to be recognised as a legitimate world title, reducing the promotion's reliance on the existing sanctioning bodies.

Zuffa Boxing made its first major statement in February when it signed welterweight contender Conor Benn in a high-profile move away from Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Boxing.

Earlier this month, four-division world champion Shakur Stevenson became the latest major name to join Zuffa Boxing.

Stevenson currently holds the WBO lightweight title, although it remains unclear whether he will be stripped of the belt following his move.

Benn, meanwhile, is scheduled to challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight title on 12 September.

American light-welterweight Richardson Hitchins vacated his IBF title after signing with Zuffa, while pound-for-pound star Oleksandr Usyk recently relinquished his WBA (Super), IBF and WBC titles and has been linked with a potential move to the promotion.

fullText:
Haiti may not have won a point at the World Cup but Sunderland's Wilson Isidor will never forget the feeling of scoring for his country at the tournament.

Isidor's strike from outside the box against Morocco was one of the contenders for goal of the tournament and, speaking in Nashville before Sunderland's friendly against Liverpool this weekend, the 25-year-old admitted that, even a month on, he still thinks about that strike.

"I've looked at it almost a thousand times, probably more. I think about it every day and people remind me every day too. It was a great moment," Isidor told BBC Sport.

"We know the Haitian people were waiting for some emotion at the World Cup. When I saw the celebrations in the country, it made me so emotional. It's the greatest moment of my career so far."

Regis le Bris' Sunderland squad travelled to the United States on Wednesday, with Isidor joining up with his team-mates having stayed in the country after the World Cup.

When asked about Saturday's encounter with Liverpool, who have a new head coach in Andoni Iraola, Isidor said: "If somebody says to me that the game on Saturday is friendly, he's lying.

"It's not possible to have a friendly game when you play Liverpool. We'll give everything."

The 25-year-old has been with the Black Cats since 2024, is eager to push on after Sunderland qualified for the Europa League by finishing seventh in the Premier League.

"The first year in the Premier League was kind of ok with six goals," said Isidor, who joined Sunderland from Zenit St Petersburg two years ago. "Now I want to score more than six goals because I've tasted it.

"I was in a bad situation not playing in Russia. He [Le Bris] trusted me in the moment when no-one trusted me, so I will remember him for life."

title: Chelsea close in on Maxence Lacroix as Crystal Palace defender prepares for medical
description: Chelsea are closing in on the signing of Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix, with the France international set to undergo a medical before completing his move to Stamford Bridge.The Blues have ag...
fullText:
Chelsea are closing in on the signing of Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix, with the France international set to undergo a medical before completing his move to Stamford Bridge.

The Blues have agreed a deal worth around £55 million for the 26-year-old, who is expected to sign a long-term contract until 2032.

Lacroix has been one of Chelsea’s leading defensive targets throughout the summer as head coach Xabi Alonso looks to reshape his squad ahead of the new Premier League season.

The former Wolfsburg centre-back has established himself as one of the Premier League’s standout defenders since joining Crystal Palace in 2024.

He made 55 appearances in all competitions last season and played a pivotal role in one of the most successful campaigns in Palace’s history.

Lacroix helped Oliver Glasner’s side lift the FA Cup before adding the UEFA Conference League and Community Shield, cementing his reputation as one of the division’s most consistent central defenders.

His performances also earned him a place in France’s World Cup squad, where he featured three times during the tournament.

Chelsea believe his pace, physicality and ability to defend aggressively suit Alonso’s preferred style, with the club eager to strengthen a back line that has undergone significant changes this summer.

The arrival of Lacroix is also expected to intensify competition for places in central defence.

Chelsea are open to offers for several defenders before the transfer window closes, with Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile and Trevoh Chalobah among those whose futures remain uncertain.

Crystal Palace have already begun planning for life after Lacroix.

Augsburg defender Chrislain Matsima has emerged as the club’s preferred replacement, although Trabzonspor’s Chibuike Nwaiwu is also being monitored should negotiations fail to progress.

Lacroix joined Palace from Wolfsburg for around £15 million two years ago and has almost quadrupled his market value through a series of outstanding displays in south London.

Chelsea view the transfer as a major investment in a defender entering the prime years of his career.

Provided the medical is completed without any issues, an official announcement is expected in the coming days.

Chelsea will hope Lacroix’s arrival provides another important building block as Alonso looks to return the club to regular Premier League title contention after an eventful year of change both on and off the pitch.

fullText:
Arkady Dvorkovich (on left) and Viswanathan Anand NEW DELHI: International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich has stepped aside from his role after being included in the European Union's latest sanctions list linked to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The decision means FIDE Deputy President and former world champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as the interim president until the sanctions are lifted or overturned.In a statement released by FIDE, Dvorkovich described the sanctions as unjust and confirmed that he would challenge them through legal channels. However, he said his decision to temporarily suspend himself was taken to ensure the smooth functioning of the global governing body. Watch Harika Dronavalli Exclusive: Inside Grenke #chess win, viral no-handshake incident, and more"Today, the EU decision to include my name in the 21st sanctions list was published. I want to state unequivocally that I consider this decision unlawful and unfair, and this decision will be immediately challenged by all possible means. I am confident that justice will prevail," FIDE's statement reads.He added that remaining in office while under sanctions could affect FIDE's day-to-day operations."However, given that until a formal court decision is rendered and/or such decision is cancelled or amended, these sanctions could hinder the stable functioning of FIDE, I have decided to voluntarily suspend the exercise of my powers and duties as FIDE President with immediate effect and for as long as I remain subject to sanctions under the EU and Swiss laws and regulations."Under Article 19.2 of the FIDE Charter, Anand will now take over as Interim President.The FIDE Council formally accepted Dvorkovich's decision and confirmed that he would not exercise any presidential powers or control over the federation or its assets while the sanctions remain in force.The FIDE presidential election at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand will go ahead as scheduled.AICF welcomes Anand's new roleThe move was welcomed by All India Chess Federation (AICF) President Nitin Narang, who expressed confidence in Anand's leadership."As FIDE enters an interim phase of leadership, I extend my best wishes to Deputy President Viswanathan Anand as he assumes the responsibilities of Interim President," he wrote on X."Vishy sir has earned the respect of the global chess community through his integrity, wisdom and lifelong service to our sport. I am confident that under his stewardship, FIDE will continue to uphold stability, good governance and its commitment to players and federations across the world."The EU's 21st sanctions package targets 170 entities and 48 individuals with measures including possible asset freezes and travel bans. fullText:
Socceroos World Cup star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after police twice stopped him for speeding in Sydney on the same night.

The 22-year-old Australia midfielder was stopped in a BMW Coupe on the Anzac Bridge at 11:05pm local time on Thursday night after he was caught travelling between 86-94km/h in a 60km/h zone, police said.

He was subjected to a roadside breath test, which returned a negative result.

However, Volpato allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine when he was stopped two hours later for travelling at 109km/h in the same 60km/h zone.

New South Wales state police said Volpato was issued an infringement notice for excess speed, while his international driver's licence was suspended for six months - which means he cannot drive in New South Wales.

The police also said their inquiries will continue and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken for further analysis.

Volpato played in three of Australia's four World Cup matches as they reached the round of 32, where they were knocked out by Egypt in a penalty shootout.

Having represented Italy at youth level, he switched allegiances to Australia in May just before the Socceroos announced their squad for the tournament.

Volpato has played at Serie A side Sassuolo since 2023 and he made 24 league appearances for the club as they finished 11th last season.

Logano Turned North Wilkesboro Into a One-Car Show — and Flipped His Playoff Fate

Every so often a three-time champion spends a night reminding everyone exactly why he has that hardware at home, and Joey Logano picked a 30-year-old itch to scratch.

Logano led 323 laps of Sunday night's Window World 450 at North Wilkesboro Speedway, then beat Denny Hamlin to the stripe by 0.859 seconds — a margin that badly undersells how completely he owned the place. It was the 38th win of his Cup career and the first points-paying Cup race run at the old 0.625-mile bullring in three decades. It also snapped a drought that had stretched back to Texas in May 2025, an eternity for a guy who usually bullies his way into Victory Lane at least once a season.

The number worth staring at is that lap count. On a flat, single-groove short track like North Wilkesboro, track position is currency and clean air is king. Get out front with the right balance and the field behind you is stuck breathing exhaust and clawing at the same greasy asphalt everyone else is fighting. Logano and crew chief Paul Wolfe clearly unloaded a car that rotated the way he wanted, and on a track this tight that edge compounds lap after lap. Leading nearly three-quarters of a race isn't luck — it's a setup that let him dictate every restart and every long run.

He didn't get to coast, though. Hamlin's No. 11 hung within range through the final stage, and the whole thing pivoted on a green-flag pit cycle. Hamlin blinked first, ducking onto pit road on Lap 359; Logano ran one extra lap, cycled through, and came out roughly a half-second ahead. On a track where passing is a knife fight, that half-second was the ballgame — especially once the final stage reeled off 175 caution-free laps, denying Hamlin any restart to bunch the field or any lucky yellow to reset the gap.

Here's the part that makes this more than a feel-good trophy: the playoff math. Logano rolled in sitting 17th, on the wrong side of the Chase cutline, and left 15th and 49 points clear with five races before the postseason field locks. In a format that hands a single win a near-automatic ticket, a night like this doesn't just add a win light — it drags an entire team back from the brink of watching the playoffs from the couch.

There's history soaked into the venue, too. North Wilkesboro fell off the schedule in the mid-'90s and sat essentially frozen until NASCAR revived it for exhibition duty. Logano already won the 2024 All-Star Race here, so the short track and the No. 22 were on speaking terms. Sunday just made it official in the record book that actually counts.

And for anyone who's tracked Logano's career, the timing carries a little poetry. This is a driver still nursing a grudge over 2015, when a Martinsville payback wreck blew up what looked like a title run. fullText:
In interview, billionaire says instead of running ‘Doge’ he should’ve ‘worked on my companies’ and shares extreme predictions

Elon Musk has admitted he became too consumed by politics during his volatile alliance with Donald Trump and his brief appointment as the president’s financial axman, running the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge).

The world’s richest person, and briefly its first trillionaire after his SpaceX company floated on the New York stock exchange in June, made the confession in a wide-ranging interview with the Economist published on Thursday. He shared his positions on subjects from foreign wars to AI, and made a number of eye-opening predictions for the future.

“I got carried away, frankly,” Musk said of his relationship with the president, whom he helped get elected in 2024 with $200m in financial backing, then served during his controversial tenure as head of Doge, overseeing $150bn in “harmful” budget cuts and forcing tens of thousands of people out of federal jobs.

The owner of Tesla did not expand on the statement, but appeared cognizant of the impact of his dalliance with the levers of power in Washington DC.

In December, he offered in a podcast with Katie Miller, wife of Trump’s White House adviser Stephen Miller, that his wrecking-ball approach to the federal government had been only partially successful, and that given the opportunity he probably wouldn’t do it again.

“I think instead of doing Doge, I would have basically worked on my companies,” he said at the time.

Talking to the Economist, however, he appeared to relish the attention his political involvement had garnered, and the influence he believed he exerted. “People don’t realize that what I’m saying will come to pass,” he said, the outlet referring to Musk – at least in his own mind – as a modern-day Cassandra.

The interview, a 90-minute conversation for the publication’s video platform The Insider, recorded at a Tesla factory in Texas, was Musk’s first since the SpaceX flotation, in which his personal wealth briefly topped $1.25tn before dropping back to a relatively penurious $750bn.

He reflected on moving from “exhilaration to terror” in a single day, but was not referring to the SpaceX share price. Instead, he was talking about artificial intelligence, which he believes will ultimately render work by humans “optional”.

AI systems and robots will eventually handle most digital and physical jobs, he said, and the merger of his own AI venture with SpaceX will allow him to develop systems to perform cognitive tasks such as software programming while Tesla manufactures humanoids.

Musk, the Economist said, plans to power his AI venture with datacenters in space, which experts have warned will be “catastrophic” for Earth.

Within five years, Musk said, AI intelligence systems may surpass the sum of all human intelligence. Within 10 years, robots in the workplace will help usher in an era of such “amazing abundance” that money will become meaningless.

It was, however, Musk’s political views, and predictions, that were perhaps the most contentious parts of the interview. The UK, a country he has not visited for years, but whose politics, especially on immigration and race, have become a recent obsession, will become engulfed in a civil war within 20 years, he claimed.

Asked if he was anti-Muslim, Musk attacked the questioner, a policy of diversion similar to that which has served Trump well, and which he has employed previously, notably calling the Guardian “irrelevant” when it decided to withdraw from his “toxic” social media platform X.

“I’m against rape and murder. I’m against the imposition of rules and laws that are contrary to what we’ve come to accept in the west,” he said. “It’s a crying shame that traditional media, like you, don’t recognize this.”

He described the media’s characterization of Europe’s far right as “false, misleading and nonsense”, and argued that it was made up of “normal people” seeking safe cities, secure borders and sensible spending, the Economist said.

In an analysis piece accompanying the interview, the outlet acknowledged that Musk was a divisive figure. “His political views, disseminated to his 240m followers on X, strike many as plain-speaking and strike many more, including The Economist, as plainly bigoted,” it wrote.

“But he is also one of a handful of men who are pioneering AI and who thereby have an outsize influence on its trajectory. When he speaks, he reflects the debates they are having. His datacentres in space could power AI’s future.

“For all his political polemics, he has a record of being right about technology in fields such as electric cars, rockets and satellite communications that confounded other engineers and entrepreneurs.”

Another Musk prediction: after AI destroys jobs, there may need to be a large-scale wealth redistribution to create “universal high income” for humans.

He said he would be willing to pay “trillions in tax” then, conversely, argued that money will become irrelevant inside 10 years. In which eventuality, he said, governments should “issue people cheques”, because, he said, amid an infinite supply of goods and services produced by machines, deflation will be a bigger problem than inflation.

He also shared thoughts about the Ukraine war, in which his Starlink satellites have been used to help that country’s military against Russia’s aggression. Despite this, Musk said any peace deal should include territorial gains for Russia.

The interview concluded with an assessment by Musk of his achievements and ambitious current projects, in AI and in space, a field in which he has also made a number of bold predictions. He said in 2024 that humans could set foot on Mars by 2028 (currently Nasa is targeting 2028 for a return to the moon, which many analysts think is unlikely).

The universe, Musk said, according to the Economist, could be a computer simulation created by aliens. “The things I’m doing are so preposterous that it’s hard to believe they’re real,” he said.

title: The 'Tarps Off' Trend Explained
description: Over the last two months, huge swaths of baseball stadiums have been taken over by fans spinning their shirts over their heads, but this phenomenon goes back further than you might think. Here's how the "Tarps Off" trend started and swept the sports world.
fullText:
One of the biggest fan traditions to emerge from the 2026 baseball season didn't start with a mascot or a chant. Instead, it involved fans ripping off their shirts and spinning them over their heads in an attempt to fire up the stadium during big moments.

Known as the "Tarps Off Trend," the celebration craze has spread across college football, Major League Baseball (MLB) and other sporting events, turning shirt-twirling into a viral rallying ritual.

While most people have probably only heard of this phenomenon in the last couple of months, the trend goes back much further and riffs on the slang term "tarp," referring to a shirt, that's been around even longer.

So, where did this trend originally start, and how did it become one of the defining sports fan crazes of 2026? Let's explain.

The phrase "tarps off" is slang for going shirtless, but the viral sports trend largely traces its origins to an Oklahoma State (OSU) football game back in October 2025.

During the game, fan Trent Eaton reportedly accepted a $10 bet from his sister to enter the student section, remove his shirt and wave it over his head.

A TikTok video of Eaton enthusiastically twirling his shirt while surrounded by an otherwise subdued crowd quickly went viral. As more fans joined in, the moment became the blueprint for what would later become known as the "Tarps Off" trend.

Over the following months, similar displays appeared at college football games across the United States before making the jump to professional sports and the MLB.

The movement gained renewed momentum in the spring of 2026 after fans at a Colorado Rockies game adopted the celebration, while the phrase "tarps off" itself also became increasingly common in sports clips shared online.

The trend reached a new level of popularity in May 2026 when members of the Stephen F. Austin State University baseball team attended a St. Louis Cardinals game at Busch Stadium.

Attempting to energize the crowd during a comeback, the players removed their shirts and spun them over their heads, helping spark an atmosphere that culminated in a Cardinals walk-off victory.

Videos of the celebration quickly spread across social media in May, prompting the Cardinals to embrace the movement by inviting the "Tarp Crew" to meet the team and later designating an official shirt-optional fan section in the stadium.

Throughout the summer of 2026, the tradition spread to stadiums across Major League Baseball, with fans at games involving the Tampa Bay Rays, Seattle Mariners, Detroit Tigers, Kansas City Royals, Houston Astros and other teams adopting the celebration.

The trend also inspired commentary videos, memes and parodies, including posts showing women participating, such as one shared under the "Women in Male-Dominated Fields" meme format, cementing "Tarps Off" as one of the summer's biggest sports trends.

However, the match never materialized after Prajanchai required surgery for a lingering injury, which ultimately paved the way for this interim title clash instead.

That unresolved chapter aside, a different kind of battle now awaits, one where a stark 20-year age gap has many favoring the younger man.

Aliff is also chasing the distinction of becoming Malaysia’s first-ever ONE World Champion, a quest already backed by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

Still, Prajanchai insists it would be unwise to count out Sam-A. The ageless veteran is riding a red-hot three-fight winning streak against considerably younger opposition, fueling the case for a possible trilogy down the line.

“In this matchup, I view Aliff as the favorite over Sam-A because he’s younger and fresh, plus he has the advantage in terms of speed and reach.

“However, you can’t underestimate Sam-A. Even though he’s older, he remains dangerous. Recently, even when he gets knocked down, he always gets back up. And in his latest fight, he even knocked out a younger opponent. His physical condition is truly remarkable.”

Anticipation continues to build around this striking masterclass, a clash of styles pitting youth and blistering speed against decades of hard-earned experience.

That reality has left Prajanchai genuinely torn on an official prediction, content instead to embrace the role of a curious spectator for this high-stakes battle of eras.

“Both Sam-A and Aliff are incredible fighters, so this fight is bound to be exciting. I believe that unless someone makes a mistake first, it will definitely go the distance.

“Regardless of who wins, I’m ready to defend my belt against either of them. Whoever wins, come face me.”

Prajanchai PongSuphan PK has been sidelined since early 2026, but the Thai appears to be closing in on a long-awaited return to action.

The PK Saenchai Muaythaigym representative has attacked his rehabilitation with the same relentless intensity and dedication he brings inside the ring, and that grueling work is paying off as he nears a full recovery.

“Right now, my physical condition is back to around 90 percent, and I’ve resumed normal training. I continue to train every day to stay fit and prepare for my return to the ring, which I expect to be toward the end of this year.”

Raring to get back in action, Prajanchai is eager to run it against whoever emerges victorious between Sam-A and Aliff this Friday, and leave no doubt by unifying the throne.

Still, Prajanchai’s sights aren’t limited to one path. He’s also acknowledged unfinished business with undisputed ONE Strawweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan Di Bella. The fierce rivals have split their first two meetings, with Prajanchai eager to avenge his most recent setback, a grueling five-round war that cost him two-sport supremacy.

The former dual-belt ONE World Champion said:

“As for my return fight, whether ONE wants me to defend my Muay Thai World Title right away or take a kickboxing match first to get back into the groove, it’s completely up to the schedule ONE gives me. I’m ready for anything. I just want to fight.”

title: Tzolis completes move to Arsenal from Club Brugge
description: Arsenal have completed the £34 million ($45 million) signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. The Greece international, 24, has signed a five-year contract with the Premier League champions and arrives as a replacement for Leandro Trossard following his switch to Besiktas.
fullText:
Arsenal have completed the £34 million ($45 million) signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

The Greece international, 24, has signed a five-year contract with the Premier League champions and arrives as a replacement for Leandro Trossard following his switch to Besiktas.

Tzolis’ move to the Emirates Stadium – Arsenal’s third permanent transfer of the close season – came 48 hours after the north Londoners missed out on Morgan Rogers who signed a £117 million British-record fee with Chelsea, describing his new employers as the “biggest club in London.”

Tzolis scored 43 times in 108 appearances for Club Brugge, and lined up in the Belgians’ 3-0 Champions League defeat to Mikel Arteta’s side last season.

Arsenal’s sporting director Andrea Berta said in a statement on Thursday: “We’re delighted to have completed the signing of Christos Tzolis.

“Christos is an extremely versatile attacking player who naturally operates on the left but is comfortable across the front line. He’s an excellent finisher with both feet, thrives in tight spaces, and possesses incredible technical ability.

“Christos has produced outstanding numbers in terms of goals and assists over the last three seasons, and he’s a player who will raise the technical level of our squad, while bringing positive energy, enthusiasm, and a strong mentality to our team.

“We’re confident Christos will make a significant contribution to our club, and we hope our supporters will enjoy watching him play in an Arsenal shirt. We look forward to sharing this exciting new chapter together.”

Tzolis played 14 Premier League games for Norwich during the 2021-22 campaign but did not find the back of the net. Loan periods with FC Twente and Fortuna Dusseldorf followed before he made the move to Club Brugge in 2024.

Tzolis follows Piero Hincapie – who turned his temporary deal with Arsenal into a full-time switch – and goalkeeper Illan Meslier, a free signing from Leeds, as the Gunners’ third signing.

The announcement arrives as a boost of sorts for Arteta after defender William Saliba was this week ruled out for an “extensive period” with a back problem which curtailed his World Cup. The France international is set to miss the start of Arsenal’s Premier League defence.

fullText:
Shares in Elon Musk company fall more 3% in after-hours trading, as earnings per share miss Wall Street expectations

Tesla reported its second-quarter earnings on Wednesday, disclosing far lower profits than expected. The company’s already beleaguered stock, which had fallen about 14% this year to date, dipped further following the earnings report.

Elon Musk’s automaker, once the pinnacle of his tech empire, has taken a back seat to SpaceX. Musk’s rocket and AI company held the largest stock market debut in history last month, turning the richest man on Earth into the world’s first trillionaire, though his net worth has since fallen from its peak.

Tesla revealed earnings of 31 cents per share, a measurement of profits divided by the number of outstanding shares, less than the 51 cents per share Wall Street predicted. Its revenue was $28.23bn against an expected $25.71bn. Shares in the company fell over 3% in after-hours trading immediately after the numbers were released. Last year’s second-quarter earnings were equally shaky.

SpaceX and Tesla stock has slumped this year, with the rocket company down about 26% since its debut. Tesla has, meanwhile, suffered from the end of electric vehicle tax subsidies in the US last year and increased competition from cheaper Chinese automakers.

Although Tesla missed revenue expectations in its last quarterly earnings report, the company revealed earlier this month that it exceeded Wall Street’s predictions for its second-quarter auto sales. The stark turnaround was driven largely by sales in Europe, where electric vehicle subsidies are still in place and gas prices have surged as a result of the US-Iran war, leading consumers to buy electric.

Tesla’s vehicle sales are no longer as crucial to its market performance as they once were, however, as the company has pivoted towards bets on robotics, autonomous driving and AI. Musk claimed last year that Tesla’s Optimus robot, which has not yet entered widespread production and already faces a slew of Chinese competitors, would be the biggest product of all time and end poverty.

On the earnings call, Musk once again claimed that Optimus would be the “biggest product ever”, but cautioned that it faced a number of hurdles given the technological advancements it would require and the difficulties of scaling its production.

“It’s one of the hardest things to solve to make an autonomous human robot that can do tasks,” Musk said.

The company’s driverless taxi service, Robotaxi, has become a major focus for Tesla as a potential new line of revenue. Tesla announced earlier in the week that it would add Tampa and Orlando to where Robotaxi can operate. The service is currently available in parts of Austin, Dallas, Houston and Miami.

Musk has for years declared that the autonomous driving service will have almost infinite demand and claimed that millions of the self-driving cars would soon be on US roads. As is frequently the case with Musk’s promises, he has failed to reach those lofty targets and rollout has been slow.

On Wednesday’s call, Musk suggested that the slow growth was out of an abundance of caution for safety and concern that if a Robotaxi killed someone it would generate negative headlines and a regulatory crackdown.

“We’re going as fast as humanly possible in scaling Robotaxi, but while trying to ensure that we do not harm anyone at all, and ideally do not even run over a pet,” Musk said.

Only about 50 Robotaxis now operate in Austin, where Tesla launched the service.

fullText:
World Triathlon Championship Series: London

Live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website and app

Olympic medallists Alex Yee and Beth Potter will be competing at the World Triathlon Championship Series in London this weekend, and you can follow the action live on the BBC.

Paris 2024 gold medallist Yee returns after competing in marathons and more recently, the 5,000m in the Monaco Diamond League.

Fellow Briton Potter tops the women's standings and world rankings after three podium places in the opening rounds of the series.

The WTCS represents the flagship elite series of World Triathlon, with the world's best triathletes competing at iconic venues including the ExCeL London.

A further three races are planned for the season, which culminates with the finals in Pontevedra, Spain, in September.

Potter will be among the favourites to win on British soil, despite missing June's Quiberon race in France because of altitude training and finishing sixth in the previous meeting in Hamburg.

The Glaswegian, who claimed bronze in the Paris 2024 Olympics, won the season opener in Uzbekistan and came second in both the Japan and Sardinia races.

Since delivering one of the standout moments of the Paris Games, Yee has experimented with marathon running – making his debut in the London 2025 race and then achieving the second-fastest time by a Briton in Valencia 2025, running 2:06:38.

The 28-year-old began his transition back to triathlon in Yokohama where he finished fifth. But the Olympic champion failed to finish the men's race in Sardinia.

Jeanne Lehair - Luxemburg: Lehair has finished third in the first two races of the season and currently holds second place in the WTS standings.

Lisa Tertsch - Germany: Tertsch is ranked second in the world and led the series coming into Hamburg but was pipped to the post by France's Leonie Periault.

Georgia Taylor-Brown - Great Britain: The Manchester-born athlete has won bronze in the 2018 and 2019 World Triathlon Series and won the one-off sprint triathlon race in Hamburg to become the 2020 World Triathlon Champion. She has also won individual silver at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and gold in the mixed team relay. She is in ninth place in the current standings.

Vasco Vilaca - Portugal: With two first and second-place finishes, Vilaca is proving to be the man to beat. He is yet to add a title to his medal collection but he leads both the World and Series standings.

Miguel Hidalgo - Brazil: Hidalgo was disqualified from the Hamburg race because he did not serve a 10-second penalty during the race for altering the race number on his cycling bib.

Oliver Conway - Great Britain: Conway made is debut in the WTCS last year and won the U23 Championship. He is just outside the top 10 in 11th place, having shown promise by finishing fifth in the season opener.

title: How lightbulb moment in Hazard's apartment helped Sheeraz
description: Former Chelsea winger Eden Hazard is a surprise inspiration for Britain's Hamzah Sheeraz on his path to world championship glory.
fullText:
There was a particular moment that sparked Hamzah Sheeraz's boxing career into life.

As an apprentice electrician who stepped away from the sport after missing out on the Commonwealth Youth championships, Briton Sheeraz found himself fixing bulbs and sockets in former Chelsea winger Eden Hazard's apartment.

Feeling inspired standing in the middle of the flashy London accommodation, Sheeraz, 27, was back in the gym within two weeks and was signed with Frank Warren's Queensberry on his 18th birthday.

After winning the WBO super-middleweight title in May, Sheeraz is gearing up for a first defence against Simon Zachenhuber on Anthony Joshua's undercard on Saturday in Saudi Arabia.

But first, Sheeraz reminisces on the lightbulb moment a decade ago.

"I was working in Eden Hazard's apartment fixing his bulbs and sockets and my ego or goals and aspirations kicked in, so I went back to the gym," Sheeraz told BBC Sport.

"There was nothing lined up for me. It wasn't like I had such a good amateur career and it was going to kick off. I just wanted to go back to the gym and see what happened.

"After two weeks, I was asked to be a sparring partner for some professionals at the time and I did well. I hung in there and they asked me to go over to Spain to do some camps with them.

"They were signed with Frank Warren at the time and by word of mouth, they trusted my coach at the time, Dominic Negus, to be signed to Frank.

"I didn't meet him for the first two or three years. I remember when I first met him, I thought it was crazy. Here we are today."

Sheeraz's crowning moment came in a one-sided second-round stoppage win over Alem Begic in May as he captured his first world title.

But the hunger from the undefeated fighter hasn't wavered.

A fight with Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez is the dream for almost every boxer and Sheeraz is no different.

The Mexican is regarded as one of the all-time greats in boxing after achieving world champion status in four weight divisions - and Sheeraz is keen on testing himself against one of his idols.

"I'd love it. A lot of people hear me say it," said Sheeraz, whose record sits at 23-0-1.

"I'm under no illusion that he chooses who he fights because he's earned the right, let's be honest. Props to him.

"It'd be a pinch-me moment if I got to fight him. I've been watching this guy since I was a kid, trying to learn from him and now you get the opportunity to fight him.

"It goes back to the saying of when your idols become your rivals."

Sheeraz has never been short of confidence and he is adamant he is on the route to greatness.

"I know that I'm here for a reason," he added.

"My hard work has taken me this far. God has taken me this far. My team and family have taken me this far.

"I believe that my true calling has yet to come. I can feel it coming."

title: Football fans believe Inter Miami exposed Lionel Messi’s reason for crying after FIFA World Cup
description: After seeing Inter Miami’s blunder against the Chicago Fire, many fans are convinced that Lionel Messi isn’t going to be happy to return to the team. Messi is set to miss some time from Inter Miami as he recovers and rests following a gruelling FIFA World Cup campaign.
fullText:
After seeing Inter Miami’s blunder against the Chicago Fire, many fans are convinced that Lionel Messi isn’t going to be happy to return to the team.

Messi is set to miss some time from Inter Miami as he recovers and rests following a gruelling FIFA World Cup campaign.

But after seeing Rocco Novo, the Argentine goalkeeper for Inter Miami’s mistake against the Chicago Fire, he might want to extend his time away from the team.

During Inter Miami’s game against the Chicago Fire, Rocco Novo asked Facundo Mura to pass him the ball as the Fire players continued to press high up the field.

However, as he tried to clear the ball, Novo completely mistimed his kick, and it resulted in an own-goal that gave the Fire a 1-0 lead.

As soon as the clip of this incident emerged on X, it went viral as many fans remarked on the level of play in the MLS, less than a week after one of the best FIFA World Cup campaigns came to an end.

One fan wrote, “Messi wasn’t crying because he lost the World Cup, he was crying because he knew he had to go back to this.”

Another fan continued the joke, adding, “Is he just playing in MLS for s—- and giggles or what?”

A third fan used this as an opportunity to praise Messi, noting, “Dawg, Messi has been carrying s— players all his life!”

“You mean go back to this freedom? Weak league, everybody gets goals and assists, defenders keep making mistakes,” wrote a fourth fan who suggested Messi enjoys the seemingly low level of play in the MLS.

A fifth fan remarked, “Bro won the World Cup and 8 Ballon d’Ors just to play against Chicago Fire in 95°F heat on a Tuesday afternoon.”

And one final fan lamented Messi not playing in the top leagues in Europe, saying, “Such a shame, man, should’ve been in Europe this whole time.”

Coming into the tournament, few could have predicted Lionel Messi to have the kind of campaign that he did with Argentina.

Not only did he help lead Argentina back to the World Cup final, but he also did so while still being the best player on the team by a comfortable margin at 39 years of age.

Many people had presumed that Messi would be a diminished version of himself at this age and wouldn’t deliver the performances we saw from him in his prime.

But the magician from Rosario managed to bag eight goals and four assists in the tournament. And even though his performance in the final against Spain was unremarkable, it doesn’t take away from his stellar campaign.

Many fans believe that Messi reminded the world that, even at his age and after playing in the MLS, he is still one of the best players in the world and could easily thrive at the highest level.

Perhaps he finds an opportunity to return to FC Barcelona before he ends his career, as such a legendary chapter of his career ending on such a sour note won’t sit right with him in the long run.

description: As the fifth anniversary of Newcastle United's Saudi-led takeover approaches in October, the club clearly has work to do on and off the field. fullText:
As the fifth anniversary of Newcastle United's Saudi-led takeover approaches in October, the club clearly has work to do on and off the field.

Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan set out to be "number one", while chief executive David Hopkinson's aim was to be "in the debate about being the top club in the world" by 2030 - but Newcastle need the infrastructure to match.

An announcement is awaited on plans for a new state-of-the-art training ground after a site was identified in Woolsington near Newcastle Airport.

The club have stressed the importance of taking time to make the right decision when it comes to either expanding St James' Park or building a new stadium, which will be key to boosting revenue.

To consistently compete, however, there is little margin for error.

Newcastle needed to see more of an immediate return from their £100m-plus net spend last summer, for example, but defender Malick Thiaw has been the only unquestioned success.

The club are also counting the cost of a bruising 12th-placed finish last season after missing out on Europe.

Most pertinently, after breaching Uefa's financial sustainability regulations, Newcastle have entered into a three-year settlement with European football's governing body.

Raising funds through the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively was therefore crucial in order for the club to have the ability to reinvest this summer.

Three key players have now left in less than 12 months, though, which has weakened the side considerably, following Alexander Isak's painful £125m departure to Liverpool last summer.

Newcastle do not want to lose another big name in Bruno Guimaraes, but the captain's future is uncertain after he intimated he wished to join Arsenal.

Whatever happens, trading will remain a key part of the club's strategy in the coming years - and there has been a shift in approach with incomings too.

Further reinforcements are sorely needed but all of the club's arrivals this summer - goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, midfielder Sean Steur and winger Bazoumana Toure - have been aged 20 and under, and from the continent.

The trio have immense potential and in the right hands could flourish, but they will need time.

It feels like the same could be said for the project as a whole right now.

title: Arsenal consider two centre-backs as cover for William Saliba after major injury blow
description: The Gunners are willing to spend big on a centre-back as cover for Saliba, who is expected to miss significant time despite not needing surgery to fix a back problem sustained during the World Cup with France
fullText:
Arsenal are looking into a significant investment at centre-back with William Saliba expected to be out long-term following a major injury blow.

The France centre-back has returned from the World Cup with a back injury and while surgery is not required, he is expected to be out for an extended period.

The Independent understands that the Gunners will therefore pursue a new centre-back in the coming weeks as cover and are prepared to spend big to add depth to the position, rather than bring in a player on loan.

Although there is cover for Saliba in the shape of Piero Hincapie, Riccardo Califiori, Jurrien Timber, Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White, some of that group’s own injury issues and Mikel Arteta’s previous preference to avoid shifting his first-choice full-backs has led to a decision to spend again at centre-back this summer.

The Independent understands Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa and John Stones, available on a free transfer after his Man City contract expired, are both being considered.

The new signing will immediately have the opportunity to partner Gabriel Magalhaes as the champions begin their Premier League title defence.

An Arsenal statement on Wednesday confirmed: “Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation. Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

“William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period. Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible.”

Arsenal could also receive significant compensation from Fifa due to Saliba’s injury occurring during the World Cup, with Fifa stating that “players can receive up to $7.5m (£5.6m) per accident, paid daily for a maximum of 365 days after the first 28 days of absence. Payments are calculated on the player's fixed salary only, excluding bonuses or other variable pay.”

Arsenal are expected to spend in other departments too, having missed out on Morgan Rogers after walking away from talks with Aston Villa once the price reached £117m, with Chelsea swooping in to sign the England star.

In addition to a new centre-back and a starting winger, Arsenal could add further depth in the wide areas given Leandro Trossard’s move to Besiktas.

The Gunners play Man City in the Community Shield on 16 August in Cardiff before entertaining Coventry on 21 August to kick off their league campaign.

title: Fans accuse Donald Trump of lying about his height after World Cup moment with Spain’s Rodri
description: World Cup fans are making fun of US President Donald Trump. The 2026 FIFA World Cup concluded with Spain being crowned as the champions of the world for the second time in the tournament’s history.
fullText:
World Cup fans are making fun of US President Donald Trump.

The 2026 FIFA World Cup concluded with Spain being crowned as the champions of the world for the second time in the tournament’s history.

Since the final was held in the US, it was President Donald Trump who handed the trophy and medals to Spain after they registered a 1-0 win over Argentina.
